Installation, dependency setup, host enabling, personal settings, schedules, credentials, listeners, commits and external writes retain their applicable explicit permission gates. A local draft is not a PR or verified app. Read the linked adapted workflow in full before its step; a missing required companion remains a blocked gate.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\npstack works best when you stop micromanaging the agent. You describe what you want and how you'\\\\''ll know it'\\\\''s done. `/poteto-mode` picks the playbook, runs the other skills as the steps need them, and shows you the evidence. This guide teaches that habit with realistic prompts.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nHere'\\\\''s what you'\\\\''ll learn:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. [Set up pstack](./01-setup.md). Install the plugin and pick your models.\\\\\\\\n2. [Route work through `/poteto-mode`](./02-poteto-mode.md). Give it a goal and watch it pick a playbook.\\\\\\\\n3. [Understand the code](./03-understand.md). A read-only investigation, then `/how`, `/why`, `/teach`, and `/recall` before you edit anything.\\\\\\\\n4. [Design the change](./04-design.md). `/architect`, `/arena`, `/swarm`, `/interrogate`, prototypes, and plans before code locks in a shape.\\\\\\\\n5. [Build and clean the change](./05-build-and-clean.md). The build playbooks, `/tdd`, `/unslop`, and `/no-comments`.\\\\\\\\n6. [Verify and ship](./06-verify-and-ship.md). Prove behavior on the real app, vet numbers with `/benchmark-checklist`, then open a focused PR and drive it to merged.\\\\\\\\n7. [Run work while you sleep](./07-overnight.md). Trust before loops, an overnight contract, a decision log you can audit, and Projects and automations that scale past one agent.\\\\\\\\n8. [Steer with principle names](./08-principles.md). The 24 names that redirect an agent mid-task.\\\\\\\\n9. [Make it yours](./09-make-it-yours.md). Your own mode, `/correct` for repeated mistakes, and how to test a skill change.\\\\\\\\n10. [Recipes and pitfalls](./10-recipes-and-pitfalls.md). Prompts to copy and mistakes to skip.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRead the pages in order the first time. After that, each page stands alone.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWhen you'\\\\''re stuck, or can'\\\\''t tell which skill fits, type [`/poteto-help`](../../skills/poteto-help/SKILL.md) with your question:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\n/poteto-help which skill should i use to review this branch?\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIt answers, hands you a prompt to send, and links the skill or guide page the answer came from. It doesn'\\\\''t start the work, because a pstack run spends real tokens, so you send the prompt when you'\\\\''re ready. It runs only when you type it.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## If you only remember one thing\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nGive the agent a goal and a way to check it, in your own words:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode the export writes duplicate rows when a retry lands mid-run. repro first, then fix and verify.\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nYou don'\\\\''t need to name a playbook or list skills. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"repro first\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" and a checkable outcome are all the routing signal `/poteto-mode` needs. It matches the Bug fix playbook, copies the steps into a todo list, and calls the right skills as each step fires.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nNext: [Set up pstack](./01-setup.md).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\"\\\\n      }\\\\n    }\\\\n  },\\\\n  {\\\\n    \\\\\\\"key\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"contracts\\\\\\\",\\\\n    \\\\\\\"record\\\\\\\": {\\\\n      \\\\\\\"tool\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"exec_command\\\\\\\",\\\\n      \\\\\\\"arguments\\\\\\\": {\\\\n        \\\\\\\"cmd\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"cat references/host-capabilities.md references/model-roles.md references/workflow-ownership.md docs/setup/codex.md skills/setup-pstack/SKILL.md skills/unslop/SKILL.md\\\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\\\"workdir\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3\\\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\\\"max_output_tokens\\\\\\\": 14000\\\\n      },\\\\n      \\\\\\\"return\\\\\\\": {\\\\n        \\\\\\\"chunk_id\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"f29de9\\\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\\\"wall_time_seconds\\\\\\\": 0.000005958,\\\\n        \\\\\\\"exit_code\\\\\\\": 0,\\\\n        \\\\\\\"original_token_count\\\\\\\": 6970,\\\\n        \\\\\\\"output\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"# Discover capabilities in the current session\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRead the tools exposed to this session before assigning work. Cached official-subagents.txt is documentation context; it proves no operation succeeded. Local agent configuration is not portable plugin configuration.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRecord each binding as `{operation, tool, exposed, succeeded, evidence, limits}`. `tool` is the exact exposed identifier or null when absent. `succeeded` is true only after observing a result. Keep failed and unavailable bindings. Successful bindings become `successfulOperations` in host evidence, with a root-relative evidence file. The operation labels below describe purposes, never callable APIs.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Operation | Discovery and observation required |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| spawn | Find an exposed independent-worker operation; retain returned worker identity and exact assigned revision. |\\\\\\\\n| follow-up | Find the operation that sends input to that worker; observe acceptance by the same identity. |\\\\\\\\n| wait | Find the operation that waits for worker state; retain terminal or interrupted state. |\\\\\\\\n| inspect-result | Read the worker result and its referenced artifacts; a wait notification alone is insufficient. |\\\\\\\\n| stop | Observe cancellation or termination through the exposed operation. |\\\\\\\\n| read | Observe the requested file content through the available file tool. |\\\\\\\\n| isolated-write | Observe a write within the worker'\\\\''s assigned path and permissions. |\\\\\\\\n| history | Observe available prior turns or records; declare gaps explicitly. |\\\\\\\\n| execution | Observe command execution with exit status and output. |\\\\\\\\n| persistence | Write and read an authorized durable record; a claimed save is insufficient. |\\\\\\\\n| external-write | Record explicit authorization and action identity; inspect the result before replay. |\\\\\\\\n| resolve-ownership | Observe distinct owned paths before contested writes. |\\\\\\\\n| inspect-terminal | Observe the worker'\\\\''s terminal state after stop. |\\\\\\\\n| quarantine-artifacts | Observe partial artifacts withheld from integration. |\\\\\\\\n| inspect-prior-action | Read the interrupted action identity and prior outcome. |\\\\\\\\n| inspect-destination | Observe the destination state for that action identity. |\\\\\\\\n| safe-recovery | Observe explicitly authorized idempotent recovery after identity and destination inspection. |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nNo default API names are assigned here. Tool names differ by host and session. An exposed tool may still be denied or fail. Record requested and actual models only when observed; otherwise use `unknown`. A requested model never proves the actual model.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nA denied or unavailable operation blocks the branch that requires it. Sequential substitution for required independent work is reduced capability and uses `reduced-pass`; ordinary direct completion can fully pass. Missing persistence limits session pickup even when current work succeeds. Preserve user authorization and host permission boundaries through every fallback.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWorker passes require observed spawn and result inspection. Each registry entry declares `requiredObservations` for `pass` and `reduced-pass`; tool observations need exposed bindings and existing evidence artifacts; native text observations use the separate reviewed native record below. Full cancellation requires stop, terminal inspection and artifact quarantine. Full persistence requires durable write and readback. Full interrupted-action recovery requires prior identity inspection, destination inspection, safe recovery, explicit external permission and a recorded prior action identity even when no external-write observation is listed.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPermission checks follow performed operations. Isolated writes and persistence require granted writes. External writes and safe recovery require granted external permission and prior identity. Authorized read-only reductions may retain denied writes; their limits must preserve denied or unavailable permissions. Required observations remain applicable to those reductions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nHost evidence is stored as object or array JSON files under `docs/parity/evidence/`. Required fields are defined by `docs/parity/evidence.schema.json`. Artifacts and operation evidence must be existing files inside the tested root. Test fixtures belong in `tests/` and prove validator behavior only.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRun `python3 tools/validate_evidence.py --root . --commit <tested-package-commit>` through Bun, for example `bun -e '\\\\''const p=Bun.spawnSync([\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"python3\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"-B\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tools/validate_evidence.py\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"--root\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\".\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"--commit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",process.argv[1]],{env:{...process.env,PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"1\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"}});process.stdout.write(p.stdout);process.stderr.write(p.stderr);process.exit(p.exitCode)'\\\\'' <tested-package-commit>`. It reads every JSON record below the evidence directory, prints each error, and exits 1 for invalid records or 0 for valid records. An empty directory has no invalid records and supplies no behavioral evidence.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe required registry file in `docs/parity/case-registry.json` declares applicability. Missing or non-file registry, unknown case, structural-only entry or unlisted host rejects behavioral validation. Maintenance fixtures use a temporary copy of this registry; they cannot bypass applicability. Required hosts must receive observed evidence or explicit blocked records before release claims. Structural checks have no required host and cannot populate host status. Later producers propose task-owned entries; only the coordinator integrates them. Source paths select callers through the task 3 case contract. Case definitions alone leave host statuses `not-run`.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Direct completion and recorded observations\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n`direct` means the task is completed in the current context. Restatement, supplied-text writing and complete installed discovery can pass directly. `sequential` is reserved for replacing a required independent method with sequential work and remains reduced. A text response has no invented callable tool. Record supplied input, the actual response and qualitative outcome review as `nativeObservations`, each with its existing listed evidence artifact and named reviewer. Their labels are `supplied-input`, `response` and `review-outcome`. The reviewer assesses the case'\\\\''s expected outcome; validation checks evidence relationships and does not decide prose quality.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nEach registry entry declares allowed execution modes and required permissions for each status. A grant is required for the performed action: worker spawn, command execution and stop need execution; isolated output or persistence needs writes; external actions need their separate permission and prior identity. Read-only discovery does not inherit an execution grant requirement. Tool observations still name an actually exposed tool and existing evidence. Native observations cannot claim tool discovery, worker identity or saved writes.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFull Arena and Swarm results additionally provide `inputRevision` and a listed `methodReceipt` artifact. An exposed `inspect-method` operation must reference that receipt. Assignment operations name `assignmentId` and the corresponding inspected output. See the [structured method contract](orchestration-contract.md). All positive maintenance fixtures are synthetic; none is an observed host result.\\\\\\\\n# Model selection for portable roles\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nUse [session capabilities](host-capabilities.md) before assigning a role. These [poteto](agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) and [comment reviewer](agent-prompts/comment-sicko.md) prompts are instructions supplied to an exposed worker operation. Reading them does not register a custom agent or authorize delegation.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Role | Default requested model | Observed model | Supported effort | Fallback disclosure |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| poteto-agent | inherit-parent | unknown until observed | inherit-parent unless a supported explicit effort is verified | Record rejected selection, replacement request, observed result and limits. |\\\\\\\\n| comment-sicko | inherit-parent | unknown until observed | inherit-parent unless a supported explicit effort is verified | Record rejected selection, replacement request, observed result and limits. |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFor each assignment, record requested model and effort, observed model and effort, supported effort values and their source, worker identity, and fallback disclosure. Use `unknown` for information the operation does not expose. `inherit-parent` records a selection policy, not an observed model name. Do not silently convert a requested model into an actual model.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nSelect an explicit model only from current exposed tool documentation or observed enumeration results. If enumeration is missing, disclose that limit and retain `inherit-parent`. Documentation examples are not a list of available models. Use only an effort supported for the selected model by the current operation; do not carry an incompatible inherited effort into an explicit selection.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf a selected model or effort is rejected, retain the rejection. Use an authorized inherited or supported alternative only after disclosing the changed selection. If the task requires that exact selection, stop and record blocked. A fallback never proves the original selection succeeded.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIdentical observed models mean no model diversity. Different roles can supply distinct instructions on the same model. Unknown observed models leave diversity unverified, even when requested model names differ. Different observed models support a model-diversity statement only for those observed assignments. Worker independence still requires successful spawn and result inspection.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWhen workers are unavailable, apply an authorized role sequentially and label reduced capability. Preserve scope and permission boundaries. Do not claim independent review, background execution, or full worker support from sequential role switching.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe cached documentation from https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents describes inheritance and optional local agent configuration. It is context only. This package writes no local custom-agent configuration and claims no current host model or worker support from that documentation.\\\\\\\\n# Workflow ownership\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nAn explicit pstack invocation gives pstack ownership of that workflow. An explicit Superpowers invocation gives Superpowers ownership. Do not run both controllers over the same assignment or let one silently replace the other'\\\\''s plan, review, or integration decisions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFor an unqualified request, D1 retains the already active workflow. With no active workflow, use host defaults and do not activate either orchestration mode automatically. If both pstack and Superpowers are explicitly requested, clarify ownership before launching workers or changing artifacts. Preserve the active controller across follow-ups unless the user changes ownership. A helper skill can advise the owner without becoming a second controller.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe owner assigns one coordinator. Workers produce isolated artifacts and evidence; the coordinator reviews and integrates them. Shared inventory and registry writes belong to the coordinator. Worker cancellation, stale results or unavailable tools do not transfer that ownership automatically.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nHost permissions and user authorization constrain every owner. Local structural tests, documented APIs and declared cases provide no host pass. Explicit reduced or blocked results remain visible beside the full expectation.\\\\\\\\n# Codex setup\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nStarting state for `codex-setup-from-readme` is a fresh chat without approved pstack loading. This route is documented, unverified for this package and blocked until exact setup authorization and fresh discovery evidence exist.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nCurrent official guidance describes local marketplace installation. A repo marketplace uses `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and a relative `source.path` inside its marketplace root. Restart the Codex desktop app, select that source in the Plugins Directory, install, then start a new enabled chat. The host loads a cached installed copy. Refresh can replace that copy; disabling does not remove it. Follow the current removal control and inspect its result before claiming removal. Source edits alone do not refresh a chat. This saved source review covers the Codex desktop Plugins Directory. Other clients remain unverified. These are documentation facts, not observed access in this account. Checked 2026-10-08. [Official packaging](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. From [README](../../README.md), open this guide and [compatibility](../compatibility.md). Record the candidate version from [plugin.json](../../plugin.json) and full final frozen Git SHA.\\\\\\\\n2. Inspect the host'\\\\''s actual plugin controls read-only. If no local source or plugin control exists, record blocked. Do not silently copy individual skills or change personal configuration to claim package loading.\\\\\\\\n3. Before any setup, obtain explicit authorization for the exact package copy, marketplace file, cache and settings changes, app restart, install and enable scope. This guide is not that authorization. No marketplace is created by this package.\\\\\\\\n4. Only within that approved scope, follow the documented local route above. Verify the installed copy through the actual host operation, not a direct repository read. Start a fresh chat after loading.\\\\\\\\n5. Observe `discover-package`, `enumerate-skills` and `inspect-installed-copy`. Retain the tool identifiers and evidence artifacts. Compare every root name to the [51-skill catalog](../skills/README.md). Exclude the three nested Benny skill paths in [inventory](../parity/inventory.json). Record the actual installed identity, version and exact frozen SHA in a discovery receipt.\\\\\\\\n6. Run the representative [walkthrough cases](../parity/cases/documentation-walkthroughs.json) with [session bindings](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Independent workers need spawn and inspected results. Unknown models remain unknown. Complete direct discovery can pass without workers. A fallback omitting a task requirement is reduced capability and still cannot weaken installed-copy identity or enumeration.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nUse the [helper guide](../testing/helper-setup.md) only for separately authorized development validation. Missing dependencies block helper-backed work. No dependency install, integration, MCP, lifecycle hook or model persistence is needed merely to read the catalog.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nExpected visible result is a host-observed installed package with all 51 roots and exact identity, followed by inspected walkthrough artifacts. Without it, loading and discovery remain blocked or not-run. Supplied-source explanations are reduced capability and prove no registration. [Test matrix](../testing/host-matrix.md) defines later host evidence; [troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md) bounds failures.\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\nname: setup-pstack\\\\\\\\ndescription: Configure which models pstack uses per role and at what reasoning budget. Reviews a role table using verified available models or inherited choices. Persistent overrides require a supported host mechanism and explicit authorization. Use for /setup-pstack, \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"configure pstack models\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"pstack budget\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", or changing pstack'\\\\''s model choices.\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Setup pstack\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nConfigure pstack'\\\\''s model choices per role and reasoning budget. This portable skill produces a reviewed role table. Persistent overrides need a verified host mechanism and explicit authorization for its exact destination. Reading this skill never writes personal host configuration.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRead [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). No portable always-applied host rule is supplied. A session-only table is reduced capability when durable overrides are unavailable.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 1. Detect available models\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nEnumerate the models and supported effort values accepted by the exposed worker operation in this session. Prefer a verified entitled-model API or CLI if one is exposed and authorized. Tool documentation and observed enumeration are evidence; example slugs are not. If neither source is available, ask the user for their available choices and disclose that pasted names still need verification before use. Never write or request a real slug without confirmed availability.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe aliases `inherit-parent` and `auto` both mean the role uses the parent chat model: omit an explicit model override. Keep `inherit-parent` for every role when availability is unknown. An alias is a selection policy, not an observed model name. If the host cannot represent `auto`, normalize its policy to inheritance and disclose that change.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 2. Load current state\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nStart with the inherited role table below. If the user identifies an existing supported override, read it through authorized tools and treat its budget and role values as current choices. Reading does not authorize rewriting it. Drop retired roles, such as `how critics`, from the proposal and list each dropped line for review. Preserve current choices changed by family, list, or alias on a re-run.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 3. Budget, map, and confirm\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nAsk for a budget using an exposed structured question tool when available, otherwise ordinary conversation. Name the current recorded budget. The upstream default budget is `large`; the portable default model policy is inherited. Offer these source labels:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- `unlimited — max reasoning`\\\\\\\\n- `large — xhigh reasoning`\\\\\\\\n- `medium — high reasoning`\\\\\\\\n- `small — medium reasoning`\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThese labels are targets, not a claim that the host supports those efforts. Set every verified real selection, including panel entries, to the supported target effort. Where models encode effort in their slug, the effort token is last or immediately before a trailing `fast`; its ladder is `max > xhigh > high > medium > low`. If the target slug is absent, choose the same family'\\\\''s verified selection with the highest supported effort at or below the target. If no such selection exists, mark the role as needing a choice. With a separate effort field, verify the combination against the exposed operation. Never synthesize availability by editing a slug. Aliases do not change with budget.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nShow every role and its requested model and effort. Mark unsupported choices as needing a choice; actual values remain unknown until observed. Show retired lines removed from the proposal. Ask whether to accept the table or change specific roles, offering only verified models plus the inherited aliases.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPanel roles are lists: arena runners, architect runners, and interrogate reviewers run one worker per entry, including aliases, so list length sets fan-out. The arena cross-judge pool is a list from which Arena chooses one entry whose family differs from the parent when possible. Unknown families leave diversity unverified. Swarm workers is the default for each worker unless a race or comparison assigns a model per arm. Worker count and independence still require observed host dispatch under the assignment contract.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 4. Validate\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nEvery real model and effort combination must be verified against the current operation. Aliases pass as inheritance policies. Stop and ask again for any unavailable real choice. If an exact unavailable selection is required, report blocked. A rejected selection must remain visible even when an authorized inherited fallback is useful.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 5. Prepare or write the override\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe portable default table is:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\n# pstack per-role model choices\\\\\\\\n# budget: large (xhigh target; explicit effort requires verification)\\\\\\\\n# Delete a role to fall back to the portable inherited default.\\\\\\\\n# Alias entries in panel lists count toward fan-out.\\\\\\\\nfeature, refactoring: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\nbug-fix: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\nperf-issue: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\nhillclimb: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\njudgment and prose: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\nhardest tasks: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\nhow explorer: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\nhow explainer: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\nwhy investigators: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\nwhy synthesizer: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\nreflect tooling: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\nreflect judgment, divergent, synthesizer: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\narena runners: inherit-parent, inherit-parent\\\\\\\\narena cross-judge pool: inherit-parent, inherit-parent\\\\\\\\nswarm workers: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\narchitect runners: inherit-parent, inherit-parent\\\\\\\\ninterrogate reviewers: inherit-parent, inherit-parent\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nShow the whole proposed override and destination before any write. The user'\\\\''s confirmed mapping and explicit authorization for the personal host configuration are both required. If no supported persistent mechanism or authorization exists, return the table for session-only use and disclose reduced capability. Never create local custom-agent configuration or an always-applied rule incidentally, and never treat such files as portable plugin configuration.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFor an authorized supported destination, serialize through the verified host format, include the chosen budget label and target effort, use the exact role labels above, and replace the whole override so re-runs are idempotent. Preserve no retired role. Read back the written result. If writes or readback are denied or unavailable, report blocked persistence and the observed outcome; do not claim that a save succeeded.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 6. Confirm\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nReport whether the result is a session-only proposal or a verified saved override. State its scope and when it applies only as established by the host mechanism. Do not promise new-session behavior without evidence. Re-running this skill proposes an update and preserves the same confirmation and write gates.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 7. Offer a verification skill\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nCheck whether the project already has a `verify-*` skill or a harness that can drive the real app. If neither exists, offer once to generate a project-local verification skill with `/create-verification-skill`. Invoke it only on yes; on no, continue without pressing. Its [leaf](../create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) is a deferred local dependency until its assigned port lands. Missing support stays visible; do not claim app verification from the model table.\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\nname: unslop\\\\\\\\ndescription: Cut AI tells from any writing. Must always apply.\\\\\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Unslop\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nEdit text to remove AI patterns.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Process\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Scan for the patterns below.\\\\\\\\n2. Rewrite. Preserve meaning, match intended tone.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Patterns to detect and fix\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRule numbers are stable ids that other skills cite. A removed rule leaves a gap.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Content\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"highlighting...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"ensuring...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"reflecting...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"showcasing...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"fostering...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Delete or expand with real sources.\\\\\\\\n5. **Vague attributions.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Experts believe\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Industry reports suggest\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Some critics argue\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Name the source or delete.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Language\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.\\\\\\\\n8. **Fancy ways to say \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"is\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\".** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"serves as\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"stands as\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"boasts\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"features\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Just say \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"is\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"has\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\".\\\\\\\\n9. **\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Not just X, but Y.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"** State the point directly instead.\\\\\\\\n10. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.\\\\\\\\n11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.\\\\\\\\n12. **False ranges.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"from X to Y\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" where X and Y aren'\\\\''t on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Style\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.\\\\\\\\n14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"If you'\\\\''re coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.\\\\\\\\n15. **Boldface overuse.** Don'\\\\''t bold every proper noun or acronym.\\\\\\\\n16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"**Performance:** Performance improved...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\") is fine, not a tell.\\\\\\\\n17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.\\\\\\\\n18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.\\\\\\\\n19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Communication artifacts\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n20. **Chatbot phrases.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"I hope this helps!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Let me know if...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Of course!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Certainly!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Found the smoking gun!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Remove.\\\\\\\\n22. **Sycophantic tone.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Great question! You'\\\\''re absolutely right!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Respond directly.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Filler\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n23. **Filler phrases.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"In order to\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"To\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Due to the fact that\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Because\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"It is important to note that\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" gets deleted.\\\\\\\\n24. **Excessive hedging.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"could potentially possibly be argued that it might\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"may\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\".\\\\\\\\n25. **Generic conclusions.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"The future looks bright.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" State specific plans or facts.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Jargon\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"API surface\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Substrate\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"base\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Wedge in\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"add\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Vector\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"way\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"method\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Gold-plating\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"more than the job needs\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Ratchet\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes the mechanism'\\\\''s real name or \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"a limit that only tightens\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Evacuate\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"move out\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Endgame\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the last phase\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Pick the concrete word.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Plain speech\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the database stays close at hand\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"SQL you can read\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"types that follow your schema\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"a column rename fails the build\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can'\\\\''t restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project'\\\\''s docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.\\\\\\\\n28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.\\\\\\\\n29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"is/are/was/were + past participle\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" and name the actor: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"queries are validated\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the compiler validates queries\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the file is parsed by the loader\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the loader parses the file\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn'\\\\''t matter.\\\\\\\\n30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"runs quickly\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"is fast\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" or the number. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"significantly improves\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes the measured delta. An adverb propping up a weak verb means the verb is wrong.\\\\\\\\n31. **Prefer the plain word.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"utilize\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"leverage\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"facilitate\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"help\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"numerous\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"many\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"in the event that\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"if\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.\\\\\\\\n32. **Mannered prose.** Metaphor or flourish where a literal phrase exists: aphorisms (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"wire it or delete it\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"), rhetorical fragments for effect, personified code (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the plan holds it\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"), figurative verbs (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"rides along\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"stands on\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"), stock framing phrases. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"A dial worth turning\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"a parameter worth varying\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Say what you mean. Rule 26 covers the metaphor nouns.\\\\\\\\n33. **Over-compression.** Dropped articles, verbless fragments, symbol-speak, and abbreviations that make the reader decode instead of read. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Parser rejects bad date → exit 2, no write\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"The parser rejects a bad date, exits with code 2, and writes nothing.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Write whole sentences with their articles and verbs, and spell out arrows and abbreviations.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\"\\\\n      }\\\\n    }\\\\n  },\\\\n  {\\\\n    \\\\\\\"key\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"orchestration\\\\\\\",\\\\n    \\\\\\\"record\\\\\\\": {\\\\n      \\\\\\\"tool\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"exec_command\\\\\\\",\\\\n      \\\\\\\"arguments\\\\\\\": {\\\\n        \\\\\\\"cmd\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"cat references/orchestration-contract.md docs/testing/host-matrix.md\\\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\\\"workdir\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3\\\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\\\"max_output_tokens\\\\\\\": 10000\\\\n      },\\\\n      \\\\\\\"return\\\\\\\": {\\\\n        \\\\\\\"chunk_id\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"8a7ede\\\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\\\"wall_time_seconds\\\\\\\": 0.000006125,\\\\n        \\\\\\\"exit_code\\\\\\\": 0,\\\\n        \\\\\\\"original_token_count\\\\\\\": 2664,\\\\n        \\\\\\\"output\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"# Assignment and integration contract\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nBefore dispatch, the coordinator creates an immutable assignment with `id`, `scope`, `inputRevision`, `outputOwner`, `isolatedOutputPath`, `role`, `retryCount`, `terminalStatus`, and `evidenceLinks`. Use the full Git SHA for inputRevision, an exact owned path, and an explicit role. Start retryCount at 0 and terminalStatus at `pending`. Preserve every attempt as an append-only event under the same assignment ID; update status through events, never rewrite the original scope, revision, owner or path. A changed scope or revision requires a new assignment ID that links its predecessor.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe coordinator checks authorization and observed host bindings before dispatch. One path has one writer. Reject overlapping paths before work starts; assign distinct paths instead. Workers write only their isolated output and report results. Only the coordinator integrates shared files, inventory, registry, or other workers'\\\\'' output.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nAccept a result only when its assignment identity and input SHA match, its artifacts exist, and required method evidence was observed. Reject stale revisions. Permit at most one retry for missing required SHA or method evidence, after inspecting the prior attempt and confirming the same permissions still apply. A retry count of 1 exhausts this allowance. Denied permissions, unknown action outcomes, and missing artifacts never become success by retry policy.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nTerminal states are `completed`, `blocked`, `failed`, and `cancelled`. A completion event links the exact result and evidence. Stop a cancelled worker through the exposed stop binding when available, then inspect its terminal state. Quarantine any partial artifacts; cancellation does not authorize their integration. If stop cannot be observed, record that limit and do not claim termination. Report interrupted execution explicitly.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nBefore an external action, record explicit permission, a stable action identity, the intended destination and the last observed outcome. After interruption, inspect whether that identity already completed. Retry only with authorization, an observed safe replay decision and an idempotency mechanism appropriate to the destination. If the outcome is unknown, block replay. Do not infer permission from upstream autonomy instructions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nHistory and persistence have separate bindings. Keep assignment events and result links in an authorized durable location and verify readback. If unavailable, declare the gap and offer an authorized local handoff as reduced capability; never claim unattended recovery or cross-session continuity. All host statuses remain `not-run` until actual observations exist.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Structured Arena and Swarm receipts\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nA method receipt is JSON with schemaVersion 1, kind `arena` or `swarm`, inputRevision, assignments, reviewArtifact, reviewedBy and declaredOrder. The inputRevision is the actual task repository revision, distinct from the packageCommit identifying these instructions. It must match the evidence record. The declared order precedes every dispatch. reviewArtifact records the qualitative outcome review and reviewedBy identifies its reviewer. All referenced artifacts must exist and be listed in the evidence record.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nEach assignment records id, workerId, inputRevision, outputOwner, outputPath, role, status, startedOrder, completedOrder, requestedModel, actualModel, retryCount, method, taskArtifact, rubricProvided, resultRevision, resultMethod and outputSha256. Result revision and method must match the assignment, and the inspected output bytes must match their digest. Worker and assignment identities are distinct. outputOwner equals workerId; output directories do not overlap. Integer order values record the observed dispatch and completion sequence, not estimated time. The method has positive sampleCount, sampleDefinition and order. Missing model observations use unknown. The validator requires assignment-bound spawn and result inspection, and isolated-write for output-producing candidates. A read-only judge may return its result through the coordinator'\\\\''s authorized artifact capture. A cancelled result needs bound stop, terminal inspection and quarantine observations. No operation string alone establishes a method.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nArena adds candidates, judge, rubricArtifact and synthesis. At least two candidates share the same taskArtifact, finish before a distinct fresh judge starts and do not receive the parent rubric. Synthesis has order, inspectedCandidates, artifact and verificationArtifact; it follows completed judgment and accounts for every candidate. The review artifact assesses scoring, base selection, grafts, rejections and verification quality. File presence and phase ordering do not establish the quality of those decisions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nSwarm adds partition, race, cancelled and quarantined. Partition declares requiredSlices, results mapping each slice to its assignment, and gaps. A full coverage claim requires all slices with completed inspected outputs; gaps remain explicit reduced or blocked work. Race declares rule, assignments, winner and ruleArtifact. first-pass must select the first completed survivor; rank-all needs all results; best-of retains an explicit reviewed selection. Cancelled assignments must be quarantined and cannot enter the aggregate. The combined partition-and-race case requires both methods and its cancellation exercise. The partition walkthrough exercises only its declared slices; it does not acquire an unrelated race requirement.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe three-file Swarm walkthrough requires exactly three declared slices and three completed results. Its partition-only receipt uses race null and empty cancellation, quarantine and failureExercises arrays. The combined case also records failureExercises. Each event has assignmentId, kind, attempt, order, reason and evidence, with bound result-rejection or terminal inspection. Rejected missing-revision or missing-method evidence uses attempts 0 then 1; a second invalid result exhausts the retry and leaves a failed or blocked assignment. A separate failed or blocked dropout is disclosed. These failed outputs cannot satisfy required coverage. The final assignment result metadata records the inspected terminal summary; rejection-event artifacts retain the invalid attempts.\\\\\\\\n# Shared host workflow matrix\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThis is a test procedure and capability contract, not observed host evidence. Both ChatGPT and Codex remain not-run. Direct file access, supplied documentation, structural tests and pictures do not establish supported host loading.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRead [capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md), [assignments](../../references/orchestration-contract.md) and [models](../../references/model-roles.md). Use one shared skill tree. Do not fork skills by host.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Session or condition | Full expectation | Reduced branch | Blocked branch |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| Ordinary ChatGPT without execution | Complete supplied-text reasoning can pass with native input, response and reviewed outcome evidence; required tools still need actual observations. | A proposal with omitted runtime or independent-work requirements remains reduced. | Runnable proof, app driving and dependency-backed helpers remain blocked without execution. |\\\\\\\\n| Worker-enabled ChatGPT | Observe spawn, worker identity, exact revision, isolated output and result inspection. | Sequential authorized roles when independent workers are absent. | Independent review, diversity and standing programs cannot pass from sequential work. |\\\\\\\\n| Local Codex | Observe repository reads, scoped writes and command results separately. | Local artifacts with absent external delivery or persistent wake disclosed. | Supported plugin loading and invocation remain unverified until tested through their actual host mechanism. |\\\\\\\\n| Absent GitHub access | Requires actual forge access, dependency prerequisites and permitted actions. | Prepare local PR content or recommendations. | No PR creation, live watcher verdict or merge claim. |\\\\\\\\n| Optional setup skipped | A verified saved model override requires supported persistence, authorization and readback. | Use inherited session role choices and optional verification offer may be declined. | Missing dependencies keep dependent helpers setup-required. No implicit installation or enabling. |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe full branch never follows from a host name. Unknown actual model and effort values remain unknown. Requested model diversity does not prove observed diversity. Bind tool identifiers from the current exposed interface rather than inventing portable APIs. Keep denied operations and failed observations in evidence.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nSupported loading is a separate acceptance check. Record the exact approved package revision, actual host loading or enabling operation, discovery result and workflow invocation. Read an installed file only as a file-read observation. Loading is not proven by a manifest, package path or documentation example.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFor each [guide case](../parity/cases/guides.json), record the required observations, permissions, actual output and existing artifacts under the [evidence schema](../parity/evidence.schema.json). Applicability belongs to the coordinator-owned registry. A case definition or scoped structural pass does not alter host status. Preserve full expectations beside reduced and blocked results.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRun setup and overnight cases with missing execution, workers, wake, stop, history and persistence separately. Without persistent wake, perform useful authorized work in the current turn and return a read-back continuation brief, or an inline brief if persistence is absent. Promise no work after the turn. A saved log does not prove automatic recovery. Inspect interrupted action identity and destination before replay; an unknown outcome blocks it.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nDependency setup, plugin installation, host enabling, personal settings, schedules, external writes and credentials need their own explicit grants. The operative checkout has no installed dependencies. The approved isolated snapshot 37b68c8e842b275f310ead112c0ecb7fa0ade308 passed 85 helper tests with 316 assertions and strict TypeScript with zero errors. That evidence proves only that snapshot. Pins are commander 14.0.0, bun-types 1.3.14 and typescript 7.0.2. The [helper setup guide](helper-setup.md) documents the exact historical copy and the separate approval boundary for any future setup. Future setup requires fresh authorization for an exact writable copy under Herd, registry https://registry.npmjs.org, --ignore-scripts and a task-owned cache. Ordinary helpers use Bun with --no-install and never bootstrap installation.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\"\\\\n      }\\\\n    }\\\\n  },\\\\n  {\\\\n    \\\\\\\"key\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"inputs-inventory\\\\\\\",\\\\n    \\\\\\\"record\\\\\\\": {\\\\n      \\\\\\\"tool\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"exec_command\\\\\\\",\\\\n      \\\\\\\"arguments\\\\\\\": {\\\\n        \\\\\\\"cmd\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"rg --files committed-inputs; git diff --stat; git rev-parse HEAD\\\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\\\"workdir\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/fixtures/cases/guides-optional-setup-skipped\\\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\\\"max_output_tokens\\\\\\\": 4000\\\\n      },\\\\n Without independent workers, sequential role work is reduced capability and cannot satisfy independent review. Unknown actual models remain unknown. Missing history, persistence, execution, app control or GitHub access blocks dependent steps. A diagram is an illustration, never evidence that a tool exists. See the [host matrix](../testing/host-matrix.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReading these files directly does not prove supported plugin loading, registration, invocation or host behavior. Both hosts remain not-run. Installation, dependency setup, host enabling, personal settings, schedules, credentials, listeners, commits and external writes retain their applicable explicit permission gates. A local draft is not a PR or verified app. Read the linked adapted workflow in full before its step; a missing required companion remains a blocked gate.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n`/poteto-mode` is the front door. You give it a goal, it matches one of twenty-three playbooks, copies that playbook'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s steps into the todo list, and calls the other skills as the steps need them. In this page you learn what a good prompt looks like, and how little of one you actually need.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![A dispatcher pulls a switch lever to route robots on rail handcars toward lit gates, under a /poteto-mode departure board listing BUG FIX, FEATURE, and INVESTIGATION.](./images/router.jpg)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## What happens to your prompt\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```mermaid\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nflowchart TD\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    A[Your prompt] --> B[poteto-mode]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    B --> C[Read the Principles section]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    C --> D{Match the task}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    D -->|Read-only question| E[Investigation]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    D -->|Defect| F[Bug fix]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    D -->|New behavior| G[Feature]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    D -->|Structure only| H[Refactoring]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    D -->|Measured slowness| I[Perf issue]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    D -->|Large work or no match| J[figure-it-out]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    E --> K[Verify and report]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    F --> K\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    G --> K\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    H --> K\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    I --> K\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    J --> K\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe diagram shows the common routes. There are also playbooks for hillclimbing a metric, diagnosing runtime symptoms and captured traces, prototypes, visual parity, authoring and evaluating skills, autonomous runs, babysitting a PR or stack to merge-ready, shipping a verified stack, running a PR queue on autopilot, orchestrating project-scale programs, session pickup, pausing safely, multi-phase plans, and worktree cleanup. The [playbook directory](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/) has the full set.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Say the goal, not the ceremony\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t write a spec. You say what'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s wrong or what you want, plus anything you already know that saves the agent time:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode users get two notifications after a retry. repro first, then fix and verify.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThat'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s a Bug fix prompt. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"repro first\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" is a real constraint, not politeness, and the playbook honors it. Watch the todo list fill with the Bug fix steps. A skipped step stays visible with `skip: <reason>`.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## What goes in a prompt\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nA useful prompt carries up to five things, and each one fits in a sentence:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **The goal.** Say what'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s wrong, or what you want.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **The done check.** It must be able to pass or fail. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Make it better\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" and \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"work on it for an hour\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" aren'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t checks.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **The proof you want to see.** Ask for the real command output, a video of the flow, the stored value, or a before-and-after number.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **What you already know.** A symptom, a repro step, a log line, or a link saves the agent a search.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **The real constraints.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"repro first\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t change any code yet\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"zero behavior change\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", and \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"let me review before proceeding\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" each change what the agent does.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nHere'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s one prompt with all five:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode the csv export drops its last row since yesterday'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s deploy. failing job id is 4812. repro first, then fix. done means the 60k-row fixture exports every row. show me the row counts before and after.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTwo things are worth leaving out:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **The how.** Say what to achieve, and leave the agent room to find a better path than the one you'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''d pick. The same goes for a list of skills, covered in the pitfall below.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **Your theory of the cause, at first.** A stated guess narrows the search to wherever you pointed. Let the agent restate the problem before you share your hunch.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFor a noisy report, such as a long thread or a vague bug, make the restatement the first step:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode read this thread. restate the underlying issue in your own words, in plain english. don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t change any code yet.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nA misreading shows up in the restatement, before any code exists. Correct it there, and it costs you one message instead of one wrong fix.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Follow up short\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen the conversation already carries the context, the prompt shrinks to almost nothing. All of these are enough:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode do it\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ncontinue\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nkeep going until done\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nShort follow-ups preserve the active owner and prior constraints. A persistent host mode requires observed support; otherwise re-invoke explicitly. [Setup](./01-setup.md#run-your-first-task) explains invocation limits.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Switch tasks with \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"new task\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nA long chat accumulates context from the last task. When you change subjects, say so:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode new task. figure out why the cache entry survives logout. don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t change any code yet.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"new task\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" tells `/poteto-mode` to re-match rather than continue the prior playbook. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t change any code yet\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" pins this one to Investigation. Without those two phrases, a mode mid-Feature tends to treat your question as the next feature step.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Give parallel work its own machine\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIf you run several agents against one repository on one computer, they will fight over the working tree, the ports, and the build output. Use independently owned worktrees or directories through authorized exposed operations. Remote placement is optional and requires observed support; do not assume a VM, branch, installation or video capture.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe upstream `/in-cloud` alias requested remote placement in its source host. It is not a portable command. Use an actual exposed authorized placement operation and report absent remote support.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen the work has to stay local, ask for a worktree up front:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode new task. branch off <base> in a fresh worktree, then port the parser change there.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEach task in its own branch and worktree means no agent stomps another'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s files. Worktrees cost disk and machine resources, so a laptop runs only a handful at once. The [Opening a PR playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/opening-a-pr.md) already works from a worktree for code changes, so mostly you only say this when a specific base or location matters.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWorktrees accumulate. When disk gets tight, ask:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode what'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s eating my disk? prune the worktrees that are safe to prune.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe [Worktree cleanup playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md) classifies every worktree by merge state, uncommitted work, and which chats still touch it. It deletes only what that evidence clears and pauses for your call on anything holding uncommitted work.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Leave it running\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen you step away, say what done means and go:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode im stepping away. keep going until the migration check reports zero old callers. log your decisions.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWork you'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''ll review later routes through [`/figure-it-out`](../../skills/figure-it-out/SKILL.md), which designs the run'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s phases and keeps a [`/show-me-your-work`](../../skills/show-me-your-work/SKILL.md) decision log. [Run work while you sleep](./07-overnight.md) covers the full overnight contract.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n**Pitfall:** don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t enumerate skills in your prompt (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use /how, then /architect, then /arena...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"). The playbook already sequences them, and a hand-written sequence usually reorders or drops steps the playbook would have kept. Name a skill only when you want to override a specific choice.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRead [`poteto-mode`](../../skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) itself for the full routing rules.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNext: [Understand the code](./03-understand.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIllustrations retain the canonical source bytes and alt text. The pictured workers, logs and controls are illustrative.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Understand the code before changing it\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Session capabilities and ownership\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThese prompts name pstack workflows, not guaranteed host commands. Read [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), [assignment and action contracts](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), and [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md) before acting. Keep the active controller. An explicit pstack invocation owns its workflow; an active Superpowers assignment remains with Superpowers. An unqualified request retains the active owner. If both are requested, resolve ownership first.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFull behavior requires observed authorized tools for every required operation. Ordinary ChatGPT with supplied source but no execution can explain and prepare drafts; runnable verification is blocked. Worker-enabled ChatGPT and local Codex must discover and observe actual tools separately. Without independent workers, sequential role work is reduced capability and cannot satisfy independent review. Unknown actual models remain unknown. Missing history, persistence, execution, app control or GitHub access blocks dependent steps. A diagram is an illustration, never evidence that a tool exists. See the [host matrix](../testing/host-matrix.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReading these files directly does not prove supported plugin loading, registration, invocation or host behavior. Both hosts remain not-run. Installation, dependency setup, host enabling, personal settings, schedules, credentials, listeners, commits and external writes retain their applicable explicit permission gates. A local draft is not a PR or verified app. Read the linked adapted workflow in full before its step; a missing required companion remains a blocked gate.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEditing code you don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t understand is how subtle regressions ship, and that'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s as true for the agent as for you. Agents usually fail in one of two ways. They misread what you want, or they don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t have the context to do the work right. [What goes in a prompt](./02-poteto-mode.md#what-goes-in-a-prompt) handles the first. This page handles the second.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\npstack gives you four ways in. `/how` explains what the code does now. `/why` digs up the reasons it'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s shaped that way. `/teach` blends both into one explanation. `/recall` rebuilds your own recent context on a topic. Each one also makes the agent explain itself in words you can check. That'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s how you supervise an agent that may know the code better than you do.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![A detective studies a machine blueprint with a magnifying glass while robots fetch case files; the evidence board behind her links clues under /how and /why.](./images/understanding.jpg)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Start with a read-only investigation\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen the cause is unclear, ask for findings, not a fix:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode investigate why background jobs time out every few hours. give me what we know, what data you used, and your best hypotheses. don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t change any code yet.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t change any code yet\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" routes this to the [Investigation playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/investigation.md). It runs `/how`, adds `/why` for questions about motivation, and returns a cited explanation. For a choice between options, it returns a recommendation with a trade-offs table. Asking \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"what data you used\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" makes the agent separate its evidence from its guesses. When the findings point at a fix, start the fix as a new task.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Trace behavior with `/how`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/how do we dedupe notifications? is there an n+1 when we look up subscribers?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAsk the question you actually have. [`/how`](../../skills/how/SKILL.md) reads the code and answers at the level of a senior engineer onboarding you onto the subsystem, with the runtime flow, the key types, and the non-obvious parts. For a big subsystem it fans out two to four read-only explorers first. For a narrow question it just reads and explains.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Dig up history with `/why`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/why was the retry limit set to five? does the reason still hold?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/why`](../../skills/why/SKILL.md) works like a detective on a cold case. It starts from source control, then queries whatever evidence categories your MCPs expose, such as the issue tracker, long-form docs, team chat, observability, error tracking, and analytics, all in parallel. The report cites everything, separates direct evidence from inference, and says \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"appears to\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" when the record is thin. A null result gets reported too, because \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"nobody wrote down why\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" is itself an answer.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe two compose naturally. `do why first then how` is a perfectly good prompt when you suspect the history explains the mess.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Actually understand it with `/teach`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/teach me how this PR changes retries. convince me it fixes the cause and not the symptom.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/teach`](../../skills/teach/SKILL.md) is for when a summary isn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t enough. It runs `/how` and `/why`, for a small change maybe just one of them, and weaves the findings into a plain explanation that builds up diagram by diagram. The \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"convince me\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" framing is worth stealing. It turns the explanation into an argument you can poke at instead of a tour.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIt works on the agent'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s own choices too:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/teach me why you implemented it this way and not with a queue. what did you trade off, and why?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTeaching helps the agent as much as you. An agent that has to explain its work must read the code and back each claim with evidence, instead of stating it confidently and moving on.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Rebuild your own context with `/recall`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/recall catch me up on the export work from last week\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/recall`](../../skills/recall/SKILL.md) mines your own recent chats plus the shared record (issues, prior fixes, errors still firing) and hands back a brief on where things stand and what'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s next. Your old chats hold context that a fresh agent lacks, so start new work on an old topic by loading it first, then hand over the new input:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/recall my work on the virtualized list from yesterday, then read this bug report.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIf you want to resume one specific chat, that'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s the Session pickup playbook below, not `/recall`.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Take over prior work with Session pickup\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen another agent (or you, last week) left a branch mid-flight:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode take over this branch. read the decision log, figure out what'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s done, and continue from there. don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t redo finished work.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe [Session pickup playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/session-pickup.md) treats the prior trail as authoritative. It reconstructs the branch state and decisions, names the resume point, and verifies inherited claims against the original goal instead of re-deriving everything from scratch.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n**Pitfall:** don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t skip this page'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s skills because \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the agent will read the code anyway.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" An agent that starts editing without a traced model tends to fix the symptom at the first plausible spot. `/how` first is cheaper than the second bug.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNext: [Design the change](./04-design.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIllustrations retain the canonical source bytes and alt text.
