The pictured workers, logs and controls are illustrative.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Design before you write code\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Session capabilities and ownership\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThese prompts name pstack workflows, not guaranteed host commands. Read [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), [assignment and action contracts](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), and [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md) before acting. Keep the active controller. An explicit pstack invocation owns its workflow; an active Superpowers assignment remains with Superpowers. An unqualified request retains the active owner. If both are requested, resolve ownership first.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFull behavior requires observed authorized tools for every required operation. Ordinary ChatGPT with supplied source but no execution can explain and prepare drafts; runnable verification is blocked. Worker-enabled ChatGPT and local Codex must discover and observe actual tools separately. Without independent workers, sequential role work is reduced capability and cannot satisfy independent review. Unknown actual models remain unknown. Missing history, persistence, execution, app control or GitHub access blocks dependent steps. A diagram is an illustration, never evidence that a tool exists. See the [host matrix](../testing/host-matrix.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReading these files directly does not prove supported plugin loading, registration, invocation or host behavior. Both hosts remain not-run. Installation, dependency setup, host enabling, personal settings, schedules, credentials, listeners, commits and external writes retain their applicable explicit permission gates. A local draft is not a PR or verified app. Read the linked adapted workflow in full before its step; a missing required companion remains a blocked gate.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nOne attempt at a hard design locks in the first shape the model thought of. `/architect` settles types and boundaries before implementation. `/arena` runs several attempts at the same brief and merges the best parts. `/interrogate` has other models try to break the result. When the job is coverage rather than design synthesis, `/swarm` fans out slices or races and aggregates their results.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe two most common design mistakes are taking the agent'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s first design and polishing a plan that no code has tested. This page fixes both. You plan through code: prototypes answer the open questions, a README or tutorial sets the target, and the written plan comes last.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Three robots draft competing bridge models at their own tables under /architect, /arena, and /interrogate panels, while a judge robot with a clipboard inspects skeptically.](./images/design.jpg)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Settle the shape with `/architect`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/architect design the import pipeline before writing any code. i care most about how callers use it.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/architect`](../../skills/architect/SKILL.md) grounds itself first, running `/how` over the code the design touches and `/why` when it moves ownership or layers. Then it runs `/arena` to produce competing design sketches, with the caller'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s usage written first in each, followed by types, signatures, and a module map.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nBy default it proceeds straight from the synthesized design into implementation. If you want to see the design first, say so:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/architect with checkpoint. stop and show me before implementing.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe design isn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t sacred once code starts. If implementation shows the same workaround in unrelated places, or types that only compile with `any` or forced casts, `/architect` treats that as proof the design is wrong. It scraps the sketch and starts over instead of patching around it.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Fan out attempts with `/arena`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/arena take my prompt to the arena verbatim. i want to compare their proposals with yours.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/arena`](../../skills/arena/SKILL.md) is the general tool underneath. N subagents attempt the same design or code brief in parallel, each writing to its own worktree or directory. A read-only judge, on a different model family when your configuration allows one, scores every candidate against a rubric. The coordinator reads each candidate end to end, picks a base, grafts in the best ideas from the losers, and verifies the result.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```mermaid\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nflowchart LR\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    A[One task] --> B[Configured panel]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    B --> C[Candidate 1]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    B --> D[Candidate 2]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    B --> E[Candidate N]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    C --> F[Cross-judge]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    D --> F\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    E --> F\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    F --> G[Pick a base]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    G --> H[Graft the best parts]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    H --> I[Verify]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe panel comes from your [`/setup-pstack`](../../skills/setup-pstack/SKILL.md) configuration, and you can adjust it per task. Ask for more candidates when the decision matters, fewer when it doesn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/arena this, 5 candidates. the cache key format is expensive to change later.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Cover slices and races with `/swarm`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/swarm check every package under packages/ against its check.sh. one worker per package. one report.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/swarm`](../../skills/swarm/SKILL.md) fans N workers across independent slices, coverage matrices, gauntlet lanes, exploration partitions, or declared race arms. Each worker gets its own scope and check, then reports `PASS`, `ISSUES`, or `BLOCKED`. The parent waits for the workers and returns one compact report with any gaps or dropouts.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReach for it when parallelism buys coverage or lets independent checks race. `/arena` gives every worker the same design or code brief, then picks a base and grafts the best parts. `/swarm` covers slices or runs a race with a selection rule declared up front. It does not use the base-selection and grafting ceremony.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Break it with `/interrogate`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/interrogate the whole branch, but skeptically. no nitpicks unless it'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s an actual bug or regression.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/interrogate`](../../skills/interrogate/SKILL.md) sends the same diff, intent, and rubric to reviewers on different model families. Model diversity is the point. Different models have different blind spots, so a finding two models raise independently is high-confidence signal. The lead sorts everything into `Act on`, `Consider`, `Noted`, and `Dismissed`, with a reason for each dismissal, and applies nothing automatically.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRead the dismissals too. The lead is a pragmatic senior engineer, not an oracle, and you can override it.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Prototype instead of debating\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNever take the first design. Ask for a few, and pick from evidence you can see:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode prototype a few options for the new dropdown menu. take screenshots or videos for me to compare.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe [Prototype playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/prototype.md) builds throwaway sketches in a scratch directory, puts the variants behind one switcher, drives each one, and captures screenshots or timings. It also works for behavior and algorithms, not just UI. Prototypes are planning with code. They let the agent answer its own open questions by running something instead of asking you, and they leave room for an option you wouldn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t have thought of.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe same idea scales up to a real design. Pair `/architect` with prototypes and keep a review gate:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode we need rate limiting for external webhooks. /architect it first, and answer open questions with prototypes. let me review before proceeding.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nDon'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t spend reviewers on an abstract plan. `/interrogate` belongs on a diff. Point adversarial review at a plan with no code behind it and the reviewers invent theoretical risks and edge cases that will never happen. Let prototypes settle the questions, then review what got built.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Write the README first for shared code\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFor a package or API that other code will use, start with the doc a user would read:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode write a tutorial for how i would use the new config package first. then /teach me why it beats the current one.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWriting the tutorial first forces the caller'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s view. You describe the API to a hypothetical user and work back to the implementation. The doc also becomes a concrete target the agent checks its own work against. Name [`/technical-writing`](../../skills/technical-writing/SKILL.md) when the doc itself matters, so a tutorial stays a tutorial instead of drifting into reference and explanation at once.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Plan after the design settles\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\npstack has no planning skill, on purpose. When you do want a written plan, ask for it once the design is settled:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode turn this design into a plan. small verifiable PRs, each with its own verification steps.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe [Multi-phase plan playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/multi-phase-plan.md) settles any remaining open questions by prototype, then writes one section per PR, each ending in proof that the change works. A passing test suite alone doesn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t count as that proof. The plan is the deliverable. The playbook doesn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t implement it, and it names which execution playbook should run it next.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFor a migration, state the bar in the prompt:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode plan the migration of our ui library to the new styling system. small verifiable PRs, each with visual regression checks. the result must match the original exactly, bugs included.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"bugs included\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" keeps the migration from quietly fixing things on the way, which would make the old and new output impossible to compare. For a project that spans many days, you can commit the plan to the repo for a while so other agents see the work in progress. Delete it when the work lands.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## How much design work does a task deserve?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou might be wondering whether every change needs this. No. Most changes need none of it. A rough ladder:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- A small, finished change you'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''re unsure about needs `/interrogate` alone.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- A change that crosses function boundaries or moves ownership earns `/architect`, which brings `/arena` with it.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- A standalone decision where independent attempts would help, like naming, formats, or an algorithm, is `/arena` directly.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- A coverage matrix, set of parallel checks, or race with declared arms is `/swarm`.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- An open question you could answer by running something, like a layout, a timing, or an approach, gets a prototype, not a debate.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- A contested design that'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s expensive to reverse gets `/architect`, then `/interrogate` before shipping.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- Work that spans several PRs gets a plan, written after the design settles.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n`/poteto-mode` already applies this ladder. Boundary-crossing work triggers `/architect` on its own, so you reach for these directly mainly when you want more or less scrutiny than the default.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNext: [Build and clean the change](./05-build-and-clean.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIllustrations retain the canonical source bytes and alt text. The pictured workers, logs and controls are illustrative.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Build the change and clean the diff\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Session capabilities and ownership\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThese prompts name pstack workflows, not guaranteed host commands. Read [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), [assignment and action contracts](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), and [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md) before acting. Keep the active controller. An explicit pstack invocation owns its workflow; an active Superpowers assignment remains with Superpowers. An unqualified request retains the active owner. If both are requested, resolve ownership first.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFull behavior requires observed authorized tools for every required operation. Ordinary ChatGPT with supplied source but no execution can explain and prepare drafts; runnable verification is blocked. Worker-enabled ChatGPT and local Codex must discover and observe actual tools separately. Without independent workers, sequential role work is reduced capability and cannot satisfy independent review. Unknown actual models remain unknown. Missing history, persistence, execution, app control or GitHub access blocks dependent steps. A diagram is an illustration, never evidence that a tool exists. See the [host matrix](../testing/host-matrix.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReading these files directly does not prove supported plugin loading, registration, invocation or host behavior. Both hosts remain not-run. Installation, dependency setup, host enabling, personal settings, schedules, credentials, listeners, commits and external writes retain their applicable explicit permission gates. A local draft is not a PR or verified app. Read the linked adapted workflow in full before its step; a missing required companion remains a blocked gate.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe build playbooks share one discipline. Say what you observed, let the playbook demand the evidence. This page shows what to put in the prompt for each common build task, then the cleanup habit that keeps diffs reviewable.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Prompt each build playbook with what you know\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nA bug prompt states the symptom and asks for a reproduction first:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode this command emits two records after a retry. repro first, then fix and verify.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nA feature prompt states the behavior and what must not change:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode add a --json flag. text output stays byte-identical. verify both forms.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nA refactoring prompt pins behavior before structure moves:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode move parsing into one module, zero behavior change. record the current output first and prove it'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s unchanged after.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nA perf prompt states the measurement, not a vibe:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode startup takes 1.8s on this fixture. trace it, fix the measured cause, show me before and after.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEach of these routes to its playbook ([Bug fix](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/bug-fix.md), [Feature](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/feature.md), [Refactoring](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/refactoring.md), [Perf issue](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/perf-issue.md)), and the playbook supplies the steps you didn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t type: reproduce before fixing, name the data shape before implementing, pin behavior before restructuring, profile before optimizing.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFor sustained improvement of one number, there'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s the [Hillclimb playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/hillclimb.md). Give it the metric, a target, and a floor on attempts, and it loops one hypothesis at a time with a frozen measurement harness. It keeps wins and reverts everything else.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nBoth perf playbooks run [`/benchmark-checklist`](../../skills/benchmark-checklist/SKILL.md) on their numbers. Perf issue vets its baseline and every number after it, and Hillclimb vets its harness before freezing it. [Verify and ship](./06-verify-and-ship.md#vet-a-measured-number-with-benchmark-checklist) shows when to type it yourself.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nSometimes you want the cause before any fix. For a live symptom, such as a leak, an idle CPU spin, or a visual glitch, the [Runtime forensics playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/runtime-forensics.md) instruments the running process. For a profile you already captured, the [Trace forensics playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/trace-forensics.md) reads the artifact and maps the hot frame to source. Both return a diagnosis, not a fix:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode here'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s a cpuprofile from the slow startup. tell me where the time goes and which source lines own it. no fix yet.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Write the failing test first with `/tdd`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen a bug has a cheap local test path, the whole prompt can be two words:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/tdd implement\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIn context, that'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s enough. [`/tdd`](../../skills/tdd/SKILL.md) writes the smallest test that fails for the intended reason, then the fix, then reruns the test. If a test would need broad harness setup or brittle mocks, the skill says so and uses the closest executable check instead. Don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t force a test where a real command is stronger evidence.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Load the TypeScript rules by name\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`typescript-best-practices`](../../skills/typescript-best-practices/SKILL.md) turns the type-system principles into concrete rules: discriminated unions, `unknown` at boundaries, exhaustive variants, schema-derived types. It doesn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t load on its own, so type `/typescript-best-practices` when a task touches `.ts` or `.tsx` files.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Clean before you commit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe [Opening a PR playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/opening-a-pr.md) runs `/deslop` on the diff before each commit and applies [`/unslop`](../../skills/unslop/SKILL.md) to the PR description and commit bodies. `/deslop` is an external companion and is not bundled. Discover it without installing it. If absent, disclose the unmet cleanup gate. Local recommendations can remove narrating comments, unsupported guards, dead compatibility paths and unrelated edits, but prose cleanup does not satisfy a required companion review or authorize PR creation.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFor prose, `/unslop` takes a target and any extra rules you have:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/unslop the readme changes, no emdashes\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''ll develop your own shorthand. The skill reads intent fine from terse prompts like `unslop that, tighten it`.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Strip the comments with `/no-comments`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nComments need their own pass, and not from the agent that wrote them. An author defends its comments the way you'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''d defend yours. So before review, hand them to fresh eyes:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/no-comments the diff\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/no-comments`](../../skills/no-comments/SKILL.md) spawns [Comment Sicko](../../references/agent-prompts/comment-sicko.md), a read-only reviewer with a short keep list: license headers, doc comments on a public API, links that explain what code can'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t, behavior forced by an external dependency you can'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t reshape. Everything else goes. A surprise in your own code gets no such pass. The comment comes back as a refactor flag, and `/no-comments` fixes the flags it accepts at the root cause. When a comment claims a constraint, \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"do not remove\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", the skill offers to encode the claim as a type, test, or lint. Either way, the comment comes out.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe division of labor is worth keeping straight. `/deslop` cleans slop out of the code, `/unslop` cleans it out of prose, and `/no-comments` hands the comments to a reviewer who didn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t write them.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n**Pitfall:** cleanup is not optional polish. A diff with narrating comments and defensive dead weight reads as unfinished to reviewers, and the extra code is where the next bug hides. If the diff feels padded, say `deslop it` before you commit, not after review calls it out.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNext: [Verify and ship](./06-verify-and-ship.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Verify the result and open a PR\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Session capabilities and ownership\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThese prompts name pstack workflows, not guaranteed host commands. Read [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), [assignment and action contracts](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), and [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md) before acting. Keep the active controller. An explicit pstack invocation owns its workflow; an active Superpowers assignment remains with Superpowers. An unqualified request retains the active owner. If both are requested, resolve ownership first.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFull behavior requires observed authorized tools for every required operation. Ordinary ChatGPT with supplied source but no execution can explain and prepare drafts; runnable verification is blocked. Worker-enabled ChatGPT and local Codex must discover and observe actual tools separately. Without independent workers, sequential role work is reduced capability and cannot satisfy independent review. Unknown actual models remain unknown. Missing history, persistence, execution, app control or GitHub access blocks dependent steps. A diagram is an illustration, never evidence that a tool exists. See the [host matrix](../testing/host-matrix.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReading these files directly does not prove supported plugin loading, registration, invocation or host behavior. Both hosts remain not-run. Installation, dependency setup, host enabling, personal settings, schedules, credentials, listeners, commits and external writes retain their applicable explicit permission gates. A local draft is not a PR or verified app. Read the linked adapted workflow in full before its step; a missing required companion remains a blocked gate.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"It compiles\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" is not evidence. The [Prove It Works principle](../../skills/principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md) makes the agent check the real artifact before it reports success, and your job is to make \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the real artifact\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" checkable. This page covers stating a finish condition, vetting a measured number, generating a verification skill for your app, opening the PR, and driving it to merged.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nVerification is the slowest step in most agent work, because it'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s the step that usually waits on a human. Make the agent able to do it, and you stop being the bottleneck. Skip it, and running more agents only gets you more unchecked work to review.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![A prototype plane flies a real test course while she times it with a stopwatch and robots film and checklist the run; the terminal reads verify: pass, evidence: captured.](./images/verification.jpg)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## State the finish condition up front\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nPut what done means in the first prompt, in whatever words fit:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode add json output to this command. text output stays byte-identical, the json parses, both run against the sample project. show me the evidence.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNow the agent has three checks it can run, not a mood to satisfy. When the reply comes back, it should carry the exact commands and outputs. If a check couldn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t run, a good reply says \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"inconclusive\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", and you should treat a confident reply without evidence as a red flag.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nMatch the check to the change:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- A CLI change runs the real command.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- A UI change walks the changed flow in the running app. When it must match a reference pixel for pixel, the [Visual parity playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/visual-parity.md) diffs screenshots against a frozen baseline instead of judging by eye.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- A parser or migration replays a saved input.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- A perf change compares before and after profiles.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- A storage change reads back the written value.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAsk for the proof as an artifact you can inspect yourself: the failing test and then the passing one, a before-and-after video, the trace, the screenshot. If the fix already merged, ask for the same check again on main. An artifact beats a plausible explanation, because you can challenge it without replaying the whole run.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFor a small diff you don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t fully trust, [`/blast-radius`](../../skills/blast-radius/SKILL.md) finds what it could break elsewhere. It picks the one fact the change is safe because of and proves it by running code instead of writing an essay about it.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Vet a measured number with `/benchmark-checklist`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nA before-and-after number is the easiest evidence to get wrong by accident. A warm cache, a debug build on one side, or work that never ran inside the timed region can each produce a convincing speedup. Before you report or act on a number, type:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/benchmark-checklist vet the export speedup before it goes in the pr\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/benchmark-checklist`](../../skills/benchmark-checklist/SKILL.md) asks seven questions and wants evidence from a run for each:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n1. What limits the number, and why isn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t it double?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n2. Did every side run tuned the way production runs?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n3. Does the result break a physical limit, like disk bandwidth or core count?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n4. Did anything error or return wrong output?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n5. Does it reproduce over alternating runs, with a median and a range?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n6. Does it matter end to end, on the path a user waits on?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n7. Did the work actually happen inside the timed region?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe verdict comes back as faster, slower, no measurable difference, or inconclusive, with the run count, range, and limiter. It says inconclusive when it can'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t name the limiter or a side ran untuned. `/poteto-mode` already runs the checklist inside the Perf issue and Hillclimb playbooks, so you type it yourself when you measured something outside them, or when someone else'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s number looks too good. It'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s the working form of the [Explain the Number principle](../../skills/principle-explain-the-number/SKILL.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Create a project verification skill\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe UI bullet above hides a real requirement. The agent needs a scripted way to drive your app. If your project has one, great. If not, run:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/create-verification-skill\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/create-verification-skill`](../../skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) interviews the repository, not you. It works out what a user touches, how the app launches locally, what can drive it (an existing harness first, otherwise browser and CDP, a PTY, or plain HTTP), what evidence proves behavior, and whether two instances can run side by side. It asks you only what the code can'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t answer.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIt writes `<project-local-skills>/verify-<app>/`, agent-facing instructions with exact Launch, Doctor, Drive, Evidence, and Cleanup sections, plus a feature map under `features/` that indexes what the app does and what result proves each feature works. The skill ships a [worked feature-map example](../../skills/create-verification-skill/references/feature-map-example/) with a README index and one file per feature using the four required H2s. Before handing it over, the generator proves the skill once end to end: launch, doctor check, drive one feature, capture evidence, clean up. If that proof fails, don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t use the output.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAfter observed end-to-end proof, agents with the required authorized controls can use it in this repo. Missing execution or app control still blocks verification. Name it in the prompt when you want the proof in a specific form:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode build the bulk-archive action. use /verify-<app> to verify your changes and show me a video and screenshots as proof.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode repro this with /verify-<app>. if it repros on main, fix it and show me a video as proof.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nOnce the verify skill works, a [`/swarm`](../../skills/swarm/SKILL.md) can split a full pass by feature-map entry and aggregate the results. A swarm of verifiers also confirms a perf win over a big enough sample, or fuzzes the app for regressions before a PR ships.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTreat the verification skill as infrastructure, not a one-off. Commit it, so every person and every agent on the team drives the app the same way. Then [build the lever](../../skills/principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md). When agents keep writing throwaway scripts to click through the app, ask for a small control CLI that the skill calls instead. Agents spend fewer tokens, and every run becomes repeatable. A CLI that agents use well has these traits:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- A few composable commands, each doing real work, rather than many thin ones.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- A `--dry-run` option on anything destructive.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- Subcommands that reveal features gradually instead of all at once.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- Error messages that say what to do instead.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- Rich `--help` text.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- Machine-readable output, such as JSON.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhile you'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''re there, make the dev setup repeatable too: seeded data, test users, and one command that brings the environment up the same way every time.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Keep the verification skill honest\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nApps change and feature maps rot. Run this when maintenance is authorized. Any recurring schedule requires separate explicit authorization and observed registration:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/maintain-verification-skill\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/maintain-verification-skill`](../../skills/maintain-verification-skill/SKILL.md) audits the generated skill: one read-only source reader per feature in parallel, then one live pass that drives every mapped feature. It ends in exactly one of three outcomes. `clean` means full coverage and nothing to ship. `changed` means one PR of proven corrections, confined to the verification skill'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s own directory. `blocked` names the blocker. It never edits product code. If the live pass catches a product regression, it reports the regression instead of papering over it in docs.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Open the PR\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode open the pr. small ordered commits, evidence in the description.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe [Opening a PR playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/opening-a-pr.md) works from a worktree, rebases the work into small ordered commits, cleans the diff, unslops the prose, and returns an actual observed PR link only when commit, push, creation and readiness gates are satisfied. Absent GitHub access permits local prepared content and leaves delivery blocked. A built-in PR tool owns the operations it covers; failure does not authorize a CLI bypass. Five narrow PRs beat one fat one, and stacked follow-ups beat a growing branch.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Drive the PR to merge-ready with Babysit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAn open PR starts collecting blockers immediately. Checks fail, reviewers comment, trunk moves. Hand that churn to the [Babysit playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/babysit.md):\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode babysit this pr. get it green.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nBabysit watches the PR with a bundled watcher and takes blockers in order: conflicts, then review threads, then CI. Every known fix batches into one push, so the checks restart once instead of after every fix. The comment triage is skeptical, because humans and bots file real catches and noise in the same list. A real finding gets a fix, and noise gets a reasoned dismissal; posting or resolving a thread requires separate authorization. When all you want is status, ask smaller and Babysit answers without starting the loop:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode check on pr 123. anything outstanding?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nBabysit stops at merge-ready. It never merges, even with everything green, because merging is a different decision.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Land the stack with Shipping\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nGreen is not the same as safe. When you'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''re ready to land, say so:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode land the stack.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe [Shipping playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/shipping.md) verifies each PR independently before it arms anything. One fresh agent per PR proves the behavior live, and the agent that judges a change is never the one that wrote it. Then Shipping lands only the contiguous verified run from the bottom, one PR at a time through GitHub by default or Origin when its CLI is available, and reports the first PR that breaks the chain. A verified PR sitting above an unverified one waits, because merging it would pull the gap in underneath.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNext: [Run work while you sleep](./07-overnight.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIllustrations retain the canonical source bytes and alt text. Reviews a role table using verified available models or inherited choices. Persistent overrides require a supported host mechanism and explicit authorization. Use for /setup-pstack, \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"configure pstack models\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"pstack budget\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", or changing pstack'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s model choices.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Setup pstack\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nConfigure pstack'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s model choices per role and reasoning budget. This portable skill produces a reviewed role table. Persistent overrides need a verified host mechanism and explicit authorization for its exact destination. Reading this skill never writes personal host configuration.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRead [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). No portable always-applied host rule is supplied. A session-only table is reduced capability when durable overrides are unavailable.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 1. Detect available models\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEnumerate the models and supported effort values accepted by the exposed worker operation in this session. Prefer a verified entitled-model API or CLI if one is exposed and authorized. Tool documentation and observed enumeration are evidence; example slugs are not. If neither source is available, ask the user for their available choices and disclose that pasted names still need verification before use. Never write or request a real slug without confirmed availability.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe aliases `inherit-parent` and `auto` both mean the role uses the parent chat model: omit an explicit model override. Keep `inherit-parent` for every role when availability is unknown. An alias is a selection policy, not an observed model name. If the host cannot represent `auto`, normalize its policy to inheritance and disclose that change.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 2. Load current state\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nStart with the inherited role table below. If the user identifies an existing supported override, read it through authorized tools and treat its budget and role values as current choices. Reading does not authorize rewriting it. Drop retired roles, such as `how critics`, from the proposal and list each dropped line for review. Preserve current choices changed by family, list, or alias on a re-run.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 3. Budget, map, and confirm\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAsk for a budget using an exposed structured question tool when available, otherwise ordinary conversation. Name the current recorded budget. The upstream default budget is `large`; the portable default model policy is inherited. Offer these source labels:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- `unlimited — max reasoning`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- `large — xhigh reasoning`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- `medium — high reasoning`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- `small — medium reasoning`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThese labels are targets, not a claim that the host supports those efforts. Set every verified real selection, including panel entries, to the supported target effort. Where models encode effort in their slug, the effort token is last or immediately before a trailing `fast`; its ladder is `max > xhigh > high > medium > low`. If the target slug is absent, choose the same family'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s verified selection with the highest supported effort at or below the target. If no such selection exists, mark the role as needing a choice. With a separate effort field, verify the combination against the exposed operation. Never synthesize availability by editing a slug. Aliases do not change with budget.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nShow every role and its requested model and effort. Mark unsupported choices as needing a choice; actual values remain unknown until observed. Show retired lines removed from the proposal. Ask whether to accept the table or change specific roles, offering only verified models plus the inherited aliases.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nPanel roles are lists: arena runners, architect runners, and interrogate reviewers run one worker per entry, including aliases, so list length sets fan-out. The arena cross-judge pool is a list from which Arena chooses one entry whose family differs from the parent when possible. Unknown families leave diversity unverified. Swarm workers is the default for each worker unless a race or comparison assigns a model per arm. Worker count and independence still require observed host dispatch under the assignment contract.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 4. Validate\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEvery real model and effort combination must be verified against the current operation. Aliases pass as inheritance policies. Stop and ask again for any unavailable real choice. If an exact unavailable selection is required, report blocked. A rejected selection must remain visible even when an authorized inherited fallback is useful.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 5. Prepare or write the override\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe portable default table is:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# pstack per-role model choices\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# budget: large (xhigh target; explicit effort requires verification)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Delete a role to fall back to the portable inherited default.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Alias entries in panel lists count toward fan-out.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nfeature, refactoring: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nbug-fix: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nperf-issue: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nhillclimb: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\njudgment and prose: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nhardest tasks: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nhow explorer: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nhow explainer: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nwhy investigators: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nwhy synthesizer: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nreflect tooling: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nreflect judgment, divergent, synthesizer: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\narena runners: inherit-parent, inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\narena cross-judge pool: inherit-parent, inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nswarm workers: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\narchitect runners: inherit-parent, inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ninterrogate reviewers: inherit-parent, inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nShow the whole proposed override and destination before any write. The user'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s confirmed mapping and explicit authorization for the personal host configuration are both required. If no supported persistent mechanism or authorization exists, return the table for session-only use and disclose reduced capability. Never create local custom-agent configuration or an always-applied rule incidentally, and never treat such files as portable plugin configuration.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFor an authorized supported destination, serialize through the verified host format, include the chosen budget label and target effort, use the exact role labels above, and replace the whole override so re-runs are idempotent. Preserve no retired role. Read back the written result. If writes or readback are denied or unavailable, report blocked persistence and the observed outcome; do not claim that a save succeeded.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 6. Confirm\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReport whether the result is a session-only proposal or a verified saved override. State its scope and when it applies only as established by the host mechanism. Do not promise new-session behavior without evidence. Re-running this skill proposes an update and preserves the same confirmation and write gates.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 7. Offer a verification skill\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nCheck whether the project already has a `verify-*` skill or a harness that can drive the real app. If neither exists, offer once to generate a project-local verification skill with `/create-verification-skill`. Invoke it only on yes; on no, continue without pressing. Its [leaf](../create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) is a deferred local dependency until its assigned port lands. Missing support stays visible; do not claim app verification from the model table.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nname: unslop\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ndescription: Cut AI tells from any writing. Must always apply.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Unslop\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEdit text to remove AI patterns.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Process\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n1. Scan for the patterns below.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n2. Rewrite. Preserve meaning, match intended tone.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Patterns to detect and fix\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRule numbers are stable ids that other skills cite. A removed rule leaves a gap.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Content\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"highlighting...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"ensuring...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"reflecting...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"showcasing...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"fostering...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Delete or expand with real sources.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n5. **Vague attributions.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Experts believe\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Industry reports suggest\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Some critics argue\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Name the source or delete.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Language\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n8. **Fancy ways to say \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"is\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\".** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"serves as\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"stands as\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"boasts\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"features\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Just say \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"is\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"has\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\".\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n9. **\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Not just X, but Y.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"** State the point directly instead.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n10. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n12. **False ranges.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"from X to Y\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" where X and Y aren'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Style\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"If you'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''re coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n15. **Boldface overuse.** Don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t bold every proper noun or acronym.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"**Performance:** Performance improved...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\") is fine, not a tell.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Communication artifacts\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n20. **Chatbot phrases.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"I hope this helps!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Let me know if...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Of course!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Certainly!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Found the smoking gun!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Remove.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n22. **Sycophantic tone.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Great question! You'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''re absolutely right!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Respond directly.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Filler\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n23. **Filler phrases.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"In order to\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"To\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Due to the fact that\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Because\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"It is important to note that\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" gets deleted.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n24. **Excessive hedging.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"could potentially possibly be argued that it might\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"may\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\".\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n25. **Generic conclusions.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"The future looks bright.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" State specific plans or facts.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Jargon\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"API surface\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Substrate\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"base\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Wedge in\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"add\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Vector\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"way\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"method\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Gold-plating\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"more than the job needs\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Ratchet\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes the mechanism'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s real name or \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"a limit that only tightens\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Evacuate\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"move out\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Endgame\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the last phase\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Pick the concrete word.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Plain speech\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the database stays close at hand\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"SQL you can read\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"types that follow your schema\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"a column rename fails the build\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"is/are/was/were + past participle\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" and name the actor: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"queries are validated\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the compiler validates queries\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the file is parsed by the loader\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the loader parses the file\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t matter.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"runs quickly\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"is fast\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" or the number. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"significantly improves\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes the measured delta. An adverb propping up a weak verb means the verb is wrong.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n31. **Prefer the plain word.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"utilize\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"leverage\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"facilitate\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"help\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"numerous\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"many\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"in the event that\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"if\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n32. **Mannered prose.** Metaphor or flourish where a literal phrase exists: aphorisms (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"wire it or delete it\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"), rhetorical fragments for effect, personified code (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the plan holds it\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"), figurative verbs (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"rides along\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"stands on\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"), stock framing phrases. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"A dial worth turning\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"a parameter worth varying\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Say what you mean. Rule 26 covers the metaphor nouns.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n33. **Over-compression.** Dropped articles, verbless fragments, symbol-speak, and abbreviations that make the reader decode instead of read. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Parser rejects bad date → exit 2, no write\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"The parser rejects a bad date, exits with code 2, and writes nothing.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Write whole sentences with their articles and verbs, and spell out arrows and abbreviations.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# codex: guides-optional-setup-skipped\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFrozen source: f4623636a287bea2aa79c4b2234a53d20a5f193c. None happens merely because you read this guide.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Load through a supported host mechanism\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFollow the current host plugin documentation only after explicit installation or enabling authorization. The supplied official research was fetched on 2026-10-07. [Plugin packaging](https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins/) and [subagents](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents) describe mechanisms; they do not prove this package loads in this session. Record the exact host operation and resulting discovery or invocation. Direct reads of installed files prove only file access. Both host loading paths remain unverified.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Pick your models\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nInvoke [setup-pstack](../../skills/setup-pstack/SKILL.md) through the supported invocation mechanism, or explicitly request its workflow when the host exposes no slash menu. It enumerates actual supported choices, asks for a budget and returns a reviewed role table. The labels unlimited, large, medium and small target max, xhigh, high and medium effort only when the selected operation supports them. Defaults inherit the parent. The aliases auto and inherit-parent omit explicit model selection; neither is an observed model name. Panel roles are lists, one requested worker per entry, and swarm workers sets the default worker policy. Worker count and actual models still need observation.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nPreserve changed choices on re-run, disclose retired roles, and delete a role to restore its portable inherited default. Show every role, model, effort and exact destination before a persistent override. Confirm the mapping and obtain explicit authorization before writing personal configuration. If a supported persistent mechanism is absent or setup is skipped, use the table in this session as reduced capability. No portable always-applied rule or new-session behavior is promised.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Accept the verification offer, or decline\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nSetup offers [create-verification-skill](../../skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) once if no verify skill or existing harness exists. Invoke it only on yes. On no, continue. Discover the project-local skill destination before writing; <project-local-skills> is a discovered directory, not a literal path. Missing authoring or driving tools leave a provisional draft and verification not-run. In this page you learn what a good prompt looks like, and how little of one you actually need.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![A dispatcher pulls a switch lever to route robots on rail handcars toward lit gates, under a /poteto-mode departure board listing BUG FIX, FEATURE, and INVESTIGATION.](./images/router.jpg)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## What happens to your prompt\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```mermaid\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nflowchart TD\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    A[Your prompt] --> B[poteto-mode]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    B --> C[Read the Principles section]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    C --> D{Match the task}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    D -->|Read-only question| E[Investigation]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    D -->|Defect| F[Bug fix]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    D -->|New behavior| G[Feature]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    D -->|Structure only| H[Refactoring]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    D -->|Measured slowness| I[Perf issue]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    D -->|Large work or no match| J[figure-it-out]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    E --> K[Verify and report]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    F --> K\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    G --> K\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    H --> K\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    I --> K\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    J --> K\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe diagram shows the common routes. You say what'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s wrong or what you want, plus anything you already know that saves the agent time:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode users get two notifications after a retry. repro first, then fix and verify.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThat'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s a Bug fix prompt. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"repro first\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" is a real constraint, not politeness, and the playbook honors it. Watch the todo list fill with the Bug fix steps. A skipped step stays visible with `skip: <reason>`.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## What goes in a prompt\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nA useful prompt carries up to five things, and each one fits in a sentence:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **The goal.** Say what'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s wrong, or what you want.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **The done check.** It must be able to pass or fail. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Make it better\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" and \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"work on it for an hour\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" aren'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t checks.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **The proof you want to see.** Ask for the real command output, a video of the flow, the stored value, or a before-and-after number.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **What you already know.** A symptom, a repro step, a log line, or a link saves the agent a search.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **The real constraints.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"repro first\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t change any code yet\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"zero behavior change\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", and \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"let me review before proceeding\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" each change what the agent does.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nHere'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s one prompt with all five:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode the csv export drops its last row since yesterday'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s deploy. failing job id is 4812. repro first, then fix. done means the 60k-row fixture exports every row. show me the row counts before and after.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTwo things are worth leaving out:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **The how.** Say what to achieve, and leave the agent room to find a better path than the one you'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''d pick. The same goes for a list of skills, covered in the pitfall below.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- **Your theory of the cause, at first.** A stated guess narrows the search to wherever you pointed. Let the agent restate the problem before you share your hunch.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFor a noisy report, such as a long thread or a vague bug, make the restatement the first step:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode read this thread. restate the underlying issue in your own words, in plain english. don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t change any code yet.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nA misreading shows up in the restatement, before any code exists. Correct it there, and it costs you one message instead of one wrong fix.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Follow up short\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen the conversation already carries the context, the prompt shrinks to almost nothing. All of these are enough:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode do it\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ncontinue\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nkeep going until done\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nShort follow-ups preserve the active owner and prior constraints. A persistent host mode requires observed support; otherwise re-invoke explicitly. [Setup](./01-setup.md#run-your-first-task) explains invocation limits.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Switch tasks with \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"new task\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nA long chat accumulates context from the last task. When you change subjects, say so:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode new task. figure out why the cache entry survives logout. don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t change any code yet.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"new task\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" tells `/poteto-mode` to re-match rather than continue the prior playbook. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t change any code yet\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" pins this one to Investigation. Without those two phrases, a mode mid-Feature tends to treat your question as the next feature step.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Give parallel work its own machine\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIf you run several agents against one repository on one computer, they will fight over the working tree, the ports, and the build output. Use independently owned worktrees or directories through authorized exposed operations. Remote placement is optional and requires observed support; do not assume a VM, branch, installation or video capture.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe upstream `/in-cloud` alias requested remote placement in its source host. It is not a portable command. Use an actual exposed authorized placement operation and report absent remote support.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen the work has to stay local, ask for a worktree up front:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode new task. branch off <base> in a fresh worktree, then port the parser change there.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEach task in its own branch and worktree means no agent stomps another'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s files. Worktrees cost disk and machine resources, so a laptop runs only a handful at once. The [Opening a PR playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/opening-a-pr.md) already works from a worktree for code changes, so mostly you only say this when a specific base or location matters.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWorktrees accumulate. When disk gets tight, ask:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode what'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s eating my disk? prune the worktrees that are safe to prune.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe [Worktree cleanup playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md) classifies every worktree by merge state, uncommitted work, and which chats still touch it. It deletes only what that evidence clears and pauses for your call on anything holding uncommitted work.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Leave it running\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen you step away, say what done means and go:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode im stepping away. keep going until the migration check reports zero old callers. log your decisions.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWork you'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''ll review later routes through [`/figure-it-out`](../../skills/figure-it-out/SKILL.md), which designs the run'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s phases and keeps a [`/show-me-your-work`](../../skills/show-me-your-work/SKILL.md) decision log. [Run work while you sleep](./07-overnight.md) covers the full overnight contract.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n**Pitfall:** don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t enumerate skills in your prompt (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use /how, then /architect, then /arena...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"). The playbook already sequences them, and a hand-written sequence usually reorders or drops steps the playbook would have kept. Name a skill only when you want to override a specific choice.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRead [`poteto-mode`](../../skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) itself for the full routing rules.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNext: [Understand the code](./03-understand.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIllustrations retain the canonical source bytes and alt text. The pictured workers, logs and controls are illustrative.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Understand the code before changing it\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Session capabilities and ownership\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThese prompts name pstack workflows, not guaranteed host commands. Read [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), [assignment and action contracts](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), and [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md) before acting. Keep the active controller. An explicit pstack invocation owns its workflow; an active Superpowers assignment remains with Superpowers. An unqualified request retains the active owner. If both are requested, resolve ownership first.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFull behavior requires observed authorized tools for every required operation. Ordinary ChatGPT with supplied source but no execution can explain and prepare drafts; runnable verification is blocked. Worker-enabled ChatGPT and local Codex must discover and observe actual tools separately. Without independent workers, sequential role work is reduced capability and cannot satisfy independent review. Unknown actual models remain unknown. Missing history, persistence, execution, app control or GitHub access blocks dependent steps. A diagram is an illustration, never evidence that a tool exists. See the [host matrix](../testing/host-matrix.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReading these files directly does not prove supported plugin loading, registration, invocation or host behavior. Both hosts remain not-run. Installation, dependency setup, host enabling, personal settings, schedules, credentials, listeners, commits and external writes retain their applicable explicit permission gates. A local draft is not a PR or verified app. Read the linked adapted workflow in full before its step; a missing required companion remains a blocked gate.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEditing code you don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t understand is how subtle regressions ship, and that'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s as true for the agent as for you. Agents usually fail in one of two ways. They misread what you want, or they don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t have the context to do the work right. [What goes in a prompt](./02-poteto-mode.md#what-goes-in-a-prompt) handles the first. This page handles the second.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\npstack gives you four ways in. `/how` explains what the code does now. `/why` digs up the reasons it'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s shaped that way. `/teach` blends both into one explanation. `/recall` rebuilds your own recent context on a topic. Each one also makes the agent explain itself in words you can check. That'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s how you supervise an agent that may know the code better than you do.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![A detective studies a machine blueprint with a magnifying glass while robots fetch case files; the evidence board behind her links clues under /how and /why.](./images/understanding.jpg)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Start with a read-only investigation\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen the cause is unclear, ask for findings, not a fix:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode investigate why background jobs time out every few hours. give me what we know, what data you used, and your best hypotheses. don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t change any code yet.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t change any code yet\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" routes this to the [Investigation playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/investigation.md). It runs `/how`, adds `/why` for questions about motivation, and returns a cited explanation. For a choice between options, it returns a recommendation with a trade-offs table. Asking \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"what data you used\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" makes the agent separate its evidence from its guesses. When the findings point at a fix, start the fix as a new task.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Trace behavior with `/how`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/how do we dedupe notifications? is there an n+1 when we look up subscribers?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAsk the question you actually have. [`/how`](../../skills/how/SKILL.md) reads the code and answers at the level of a senior engineer onboarding you onto the subsystem, with the runtime flow, the key types, and the non-obvious parts. For a big subsystem it fans out two to four read-only explorers first. For a narrow question it just reads and explains.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Dig up history with `/why`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/why was the retry limit set to five? does the reason still hold?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/why`](../../skills/why/SKILL.md) works like a detective on a cold case. It starts from source control, then queries whatever evidence categories your MCPs expose, such as the issue tracker, long-form docs, team chat, observability, error tracking, and analytics, all in parallel. The report cites everything, separates direct evidence from inference, and says \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"appears to\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" when the record is thin. A null result gets reported too, because \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"nobody wrote down why\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" is itself an answer.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe two compose naturally. `do why first then how` is a perfectly good prompt when you suspect the history explains the mess.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Actually understand it with `/teach`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/teach me how this PR changes retries. convince me it fixes the cause and not the symptom.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/teach`](../../skills/teach/SKILL.md) is for when a summary isn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t enough. It runs `/how` and `/why`, for a small change maybe just one of them, and weaves the findings into a plain explanation that builds up diagram by diagram. The \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"convince me\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" framing is worth stealing. It turns the explanation into an argument you can poke at instead of a tour.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIt works on the agent'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s own choices too:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/teach me why you implemented it this way and not with a queue. what did you trade off, and why?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTeaching helps the agent as much as you. An agent that has to explain its work must read the code and back each claim with evidence, instead of stating it confidently and moving on.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Rebuild your own context with `/recall`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/recall catch me up on the export work from last week\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n[`/recall`](../../skills/recall/SKILL.md) mines your own recent chats plus the shared record (issues, prior fixes, errors still firing) and hands back a brief on where things stand and what'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s next. Your old chats hold context that a fresh agent lacks, so start new work on an old topic by loading it first, then hand over the new input:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/recall my work on the virtualized list from yesterday, then read this bug report.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIf you want to resume one specific chat, that'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s the Session pickup playbook below, not `/recall`.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Take over prior work with Session pickup\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen another agent (or you, last week) left a branch mid-flight:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n/poteto-mode take over this branch. read the decision log, figure out what'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s done, and continue from there. don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t redo finished work.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe [Session pickup playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/session-pickup.md) treats the prior trail as authoritative. It reconstructs the branch state and decisions, names the resume point, and verifies inherited claims against the original goal instead of re-deriving everything from scratch.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n**Pitfall:** don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t skip this page'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s skills because \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the agent will read the code anyway.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" An agent that starts editing without a traced model tends to fix the symptom at the first plausible spot. `/how` first is cheaper than the second bug.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNext: [Design the change](./04-design.md).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIllustrations retain the canonical source bytes and alt text.
