Use for /setup-pstack, \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"configure pstack models\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"pstack budget\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", or changing pstack'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s model choices.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Setup pstack\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nConfigure pstack'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s model choices per role and reasoning budget. This portable skill produces a reviewed role table. Persistent overrides need a verified host mechanism and explicit authorization for its exact destination. Reading this skill never writes personal host configuration.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRead [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). No portable always-applied host rule is supplied. A session-only table is reduced capability when durable overrides are unavailable.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 1. Detect available models\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEnumerate the models and supported effort values accepted by the exposed worker operation in this session. Prefer a verified entitled-model API or CLI if one is exposed and authorized. Tool documentation and observed enumeration are evidence; example slugs are not. If neither source is available, ask the user for their available choices and disclose that pasted names still need verification before use. Never write or request a real slug without confirmed availability.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe aliases `inherit-parent` and `auto` both mean the role uses the parent chat model: omit an explicit model override. Keep `inherit-parent` for every role when availability is unknown. An alias is a selection policy, not an observed model name. If the host cannot represent `auto`, normalize its policy to inheritance and disclose that change.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 2. Load current state\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nStart with the inherited role table below. If the user identifies an existing supported override, read it through authorized tools and treat its budget and role values as current choices. Reading does not authorize rewriting it. Drop retired roles, such as `how critics`, from the proposal and list each dropped line for review. Preserve current choices changed by family, list, or alias on a re-run.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 3. Budget, map, and confirm\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAsk for a budget using an exposed structured question tool when available, otherwise ordinary conversation. Name the current recorded budget. The upstream default budget is `large`; the portable default model policy is inherited. Offer these source labels:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- `unlimited — max reasoning`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- `large — xhigh reasoning`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- `medium — high reasoning`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- `small — medium reasoning`\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThese labels are targets, not a claim that the host supports those efforts. Set every verified real selection, including panel entries, to the supported target effort. Where models encode effort in their slug, the effort token is last or immediately before a trailing `fast`; its ladder is `max > xhigh > high > medium > low`. If the target slug is absent, choose the same family'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s verified selection with the highest supported effort at or below the target. If no such selection exists, mark the role as needing a choice. With a separate effort field, verify the combination against the exposed operation. Never synthesize availability by editing a slug. Aliases do not change with budget.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nShow every role and its requested model and effort. Mark unsupported choices as needing a choice; actual values remain unknown until observed. Show retired lines removed from the proposal. Ask whether to accept the table or change specific roles, offering only verified models plus the inherited aliases.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nPanel roles are lists: arena runners, architect runners, and interrogate reviewers run one worker per entry, including aliases, so list length sets fan-out. The arena cross-judge pool is a list from which Arena chooses one entry whose family differs from the parent when possible. Unknown families leave diversity unverified. Swarm workers is the default for each worker unless a race or comparison assigns a model per arm. Worker count and independence still require observed host dispatch under the assignment contract.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 4. Validate\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEvery real model and effort combination must be verified against the current operation. Aliases pass as inheritance policies. Stop and ask again for any unavailable real choice. If an exact unavailable selection is required, report blocked. A rejected selection must remain visible even when an authorized inherited fallback is useful.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 5. Prepare or write the override\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe portable default table is:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# pstack per-role model choices\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# budget: large (xhigh target; explicit effort requires verification)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Delete a role to fall back to the portable inherited default.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Alias entries in panel lists count toward fan-out.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nfeature, refactoring: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nbug-fix: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nperf-issue: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nhillclimb: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\njudgment and prose: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nhardest tasks: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nhow explorer: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nhow explainer: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nwhy investigators: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nwhy synthesizer: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nreflect tooling: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nreflect judgment, divergent, synthesizer: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\narena runners: inherit-parent, inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\narena cross-judge pool: inherit-parent, inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nswarm workers: inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\narchitect runners: inherit-parent, inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ninterrogate reviewers: inherit-parent, inherit-parent\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nShow the whole proposed override and destination before any write. The user'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s confirmed mapping and explicit authorization for the personal host configuration are both required. If no supported persistent mechanism or authorization exists, return the table for session-only use and disclose reduced capability. Never create local custom-agent configuration or an always-applied rule incidentally, and never treat such files as portable plugin configuration.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFor an authorized supported destination, serialize through the verified host format, include the chosen budget label and target effort, use the exact role labels above, and replace the whole override so re-runs are idempotent. Preserve no retired role. Read back the written result. If writes or readback are denied or unavailable, report blocked persistence and the observed outcome; do not claim that a save succeeded.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 6. Confirm\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReport whether the result is a session-only proposal or a verified saved override. State its scope and when it applies only as established by the host mechanism. Do not promise new-session behavior without evidence. Re-running this skill proposes an update and preserves the same confirmation and write gates.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## 7. Offer a verification skill\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nCheck whether the project already has a `verify-*` skill or a harness that can drive the real app. If neither exists, offer once to generate a project-local verification skill with `/create-verification-skill`. Invoke it only on yes; on no, continue without pressing. Its [leaf](../create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) is a deferred local dependency until its assigned port lands. Missing support stays visible; do not claim app verification from the model table.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nname: unslop\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ndescription: Cut AI tells from any writing. Must always apply.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Unslop\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEdit text to remove AI patterns.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Process\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n1. Scan for the patterns below.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n2. Rewrite. Preserve meaning, match intended tone.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Patterns to detect and fix\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRule numbers are stable ids that other skills cite. A removed rule leaves a gap.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Content\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"highlighting...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"ensuring...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"reflecting...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"showcasing...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"fostering...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Delete or expand with real sources.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n5. **Vague attributions.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Experts believe\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Industry reports suggest\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Some critics argue\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Name the source or delete.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Language\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n8. **Fancy ways to say \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"is\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\".** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"serves as\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"stands as\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"boasts\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"features\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Just say \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"is\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"has\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\".\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n9. **\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Not just X, but Y.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"** State the point directly instead.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n10. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n12. **False ranges.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"from X to Y\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" where X and Y aren'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Style\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"If you'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''re coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n15. **Boldface overuse.** Don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t bold every proper noun or acronym.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"**Performance:** Performance improved...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\") is fine, not a tell.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Communication artifacts\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n20. **Chatbot phrases.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"I hope this helps!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Let me know if...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Of course!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Certainly!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Found the smoking gun!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Remove.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n22. **Sycophantic tone.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Great question! You'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''re absolutely right!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Respond directly.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Filler\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n23. **Filler phrases.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"In order to\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"To\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Due to the fact that\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Because\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"It is important to note that\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" gets deleted.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n24. **Excessive hedging.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"could potentially possibly be argued that it might\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"may\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\".\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n25. **Generic conclusions.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"The future looks bright.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" State specific plans or facts.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Jargon\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"API surface\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Substrate\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"base\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Wedge in\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"add\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Vector\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"way\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"method\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Gold-plating\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"more than the job needs\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Ratchet\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes the mechanism'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s real name or \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"a limit that only tightens\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Evacuate\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"move out\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Endgame\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the last phase\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Pick the concrete word.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Plain speech\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the database stays close at hand\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"SQL you can read\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"types that follow your schema\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"a column rename fails the build\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"is/are/was/were + past participle\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" and name the actor: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"queries are validated\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the compiler validates queries\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the file is parsed by the loader\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the loader parses the file\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t matter.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"runs quickly\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"is fast\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" or the number. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"significantly improves\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes the measured delta. An adverb propping up a weak verb means the verb is wrong.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n31. **Prefer the plain word.** \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"utilize\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"leverage\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"facilitate\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"help\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"numerous\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"many\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"in the event that\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"if\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n32. **Mannered prose.** Metaphor or flourish where a literal phrase exists: aphorisms (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"wire it or delete it\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"), rhetorical fragments for effect, personified code (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the plan holds it\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"), figurative verbs (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"rides along\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"stands on\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"), stock framing phrases. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"A dial worth turning\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"a parameter worth varying\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". Say what you mean. Rule 26 covers the metaphor nouns.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n33. **Over-compression.** Dropped articles, verbless fragments, symbol-speak, and abbreviations that make the reader decode instead of read. \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Parser rejects bad date → exit 2, no write\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"The parser rejects a bad date, exits with code 2, and writes nothing.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Write whole sentences with their articles and verbs, and spell out arrows and abbreviations.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n      }\\\\\\\\n \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"original_token_count\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\": 2664,\\\\\\\\n        \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"output\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"# Assignment and integration contract\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nBefore dispatch, the coordinator creates an immutable assignment with `id`, `scope`, `inputRevision`, `outputOwner`, `isolatedOutputPath`, `role`, `retryCount`, `terminalStatus`, and `evidenceLinks`. Use the full Git SHA for inputRevision, an exact owned path, and an explicit role. Start retryCount at 0 and terminalStatus at `pending`. Preserve every attempt as an append-only event under the same assignment ID; update status through events, never rewrite the original scope, revision, owner or path. A changed scope or revision requires a new assignment ID that links its predecessor.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe coordinator checks authorization and observed host bindings before dispatch. One path has one writer. Reject overlapping paths before work starts; assign distinct paths instead. Workers write only their isolated output and report results. Only the coordinator integrates shared files, inventory, registry, or other workers'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\'' output.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAccept a result only when its assignment identity and input SHA match, its artifacts exist, and required method evidence was observed. Reject stale revisions. Permit at most one retry for missing required SHA or method evidence, after inspecting the prior attempt and confirming the same permissions still apply. A retry count of 1 exhausts this allowance. Denied permissions, unknown action outcomes, and missing artifacts never become success by retry policy.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTerminal states are `completed`, `blocked`, `failed`, and `cancelled`. A completion event links the exact result and evidence. Stop a cancelled worker through the exposed stop binding when available, then inspect its terminal state. Quarantine any partial artifacts; cancellation does not authorize their integration. If stop cannot be observed, record that limit and do not claim termination. Report interrupted execution explicitly.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nBefore an external action, record explicit permission, a stable action identity, the intended destination and the last observed outcome. After interruption, inspect whether that identity already completed. Retry only with authorization, an observed safe replay decision and an idempotency mechanism appropriate to the destination. If the outcome is unknown, block replay. Do not infer permission from upstream autonomy instructions.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nHistory and persistence have separate bindings. Keep assignment events and result links in an authorized durable location and verify readback. If unavailable, declare the gap and offer an authorized local handoff as reduced capability; never claim unattended recovery or cross-session continuity. All host statuses remain `not-run` until actual observations exist.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Structured Arena and Swarm receipts\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nA method receipt is JSON with schemaVersion 1, kind `arena` or `swarm`, inputRevision, assignments, reviewArtifact, reviewedBy and declaredOrder. The inputRevision is the actual task repository revision, distinct from the packageCommit identifying these instructions. It must match the evidence record. The declared order precedes every dispatch. reviewArtifact records the qualitative outcome review and reviewedBy identifies its reviewer. All referenced artifacts must exist and be listed in the evidence record.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEach assignment records id, workerId, inputRevision, outputOwner, outputPath, role, status, startedOrder, completedOrder, requestedModel, actualModel, retryCount, method, taskArtifact, rubricProvided, resultRevision, resultMethod and outputSha256. Result revision and method must match the assignment, and the inspected output bytes must match their digest. Worker and assignment identities are distinct. outputOwner equals workerId; output directories do not overlap. Integer order values record the observed dispatch and completion sequence, not estimated time. The method has positive sampleCount, sampleDefinition and order. Missing model observations use unknown. The validator requires assignment-bound spawn and result inspection, and isolated-write for output-producing candidates. A read-only judge may return its result through the coordinator'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s authorized artifact capture. A cancelled result needs bound stop, terminal inspection and quarantine observations. No operation string alone establishes a method.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nArena adds candidates, judge, rubricArtifact and synthesis. At least two candidates share the same taskArtifact, finish before a distinct fresh judge starts and do not receive the parent rubric. Synthesis has order, inspectedCandidates, artifact and verificationArtifact; it follows completed judgment and accounts for every candidate. The review artifact assesses scoring, base selection, grafts, rejections and verification quality. File presence and phase ordering do not establish the quality of those decisions.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nSwarm adds partition, race, cancelled and quarantined. Partition declares requiredSlices, results mapping each slice to its assignment, and gaps. A full coverage claim requires all slices with completed inspected outputs; gaps remain explicit reduced or blocked work. Race declares rule, assignments, winner and ruleArtifact. first-pass must select the first completed survivor; rank-all needs all results; best-of retains an explicit reviewed selection. Cancelled assignments must be quarantined and cannot enter the aggregate. The combined partition-and-race case requires both methods and its cancellation exercise. The partition walkthrough exercises only its declared slices; it does not acquire an unrelated race requirement.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe three-file Swarm walkthrough requires exactly three declared slices and three completed results. Its partition-only receipt uses race null and empty cancellation, quarantine and failureExercises arrays. The combined case also records failureExercises. Each event has assignmentId, kind, attempt, order, reason and evidence, with bound result-rejection or terminal inspection. Rejected missing-revision or missing-method evidence uses attempts 0 then 1; a second invalid result exhausts the retry and leaves a failed or blocked assignment. A separate failed or blocked dropout is disclosed. These failed outputs cannot satisfy required coverage. The final assignment result metadata records the inspected terminal summary; rejection-event artifacts retain the invalid attempts.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n# Shared host workflow matrix\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis is a test procedure and capability contract, not observed host evidence. Both ChatGPT and Codex remain not-run. Direct file access, supplied documentation, structural tests and pictures do not establish supported host loading.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRead [capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md), [assignments](../../references/orchestration-contract.md) and [models](../../references/model-roles.md). Use one shared skill tree. Do not fork skills by host.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Session or condition | Full expectation | Reduced branch | Blocked branch |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Ordinary ChatGPT without execution | Complete supplied-text reasoning can pass with native input, response and reviewed outcome evidence; required tools still need actual observations. | A proposal with omitted runtime or independent-work requirements remains reduced. | Runnable proof, app driving and dependency-backed helpers remain blocked without execution. |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Worker-enabled ChatGPT | Observe spawn, worker identity, exact revision, isolated output and result inspection. | Sequential authorized roles when independent workers are absent. | Independent review, diversity and standing programs cannot pass from sequential work. |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Local Codex | Observe repository reads, scoped writes and command results separately. | Local artifacts with absent external delivery or persistent wake disclosed. | Supported plugin loading and invocation remain unverified until tested through their actual host mechanism. |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Absent GitHub access | Requires actual forge access, dependency prerequisites and permitted actions. | Prepare local PR content or recommendations. | No PR creation, live watcher verdict or merge claim. |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Optional setup skipped | A verified saved model override requires supported persistence, authorization and readback. | Use inherited session role choices and optional verification offer may be declined. | Missing dependencies keep dependent helpers setup-required. No implicit installation or enabling. |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe full branch never follows from a host name. Unknown actual model and effort values remain unknown. Requested model diversity does not prove observed diversity. Bind tool identifiers from the current exposed interface rather than inventing portable APIs. Keep denied operations and failed observations in evidence.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nSupported loading is a separate acceptance check. Record the exact approved package revision, actual host loading or enabling operation, discovery result and workflow invocation. Read an installed file only as a file-read observation. Loading is not proven by a manifest, package path or documentation example.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFor each [guide case](../parity/cases/guides.json), record the required observations, permissions, actual output and existing artifacts under the [evidence schema](../parity/evidence.schema.json). Applicability belongs to the coordinator-owned registry. A case definition or scoped structural pass does not alter host status. Preserve full expectations beside reduced and blocked results.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRun setup and overnight cases with missing execution, workers, wake, stop, history and persistence separately. Without persistent wake, perform useful authorized work in the current turn and return a read-back continuation brief, or an inline brief if persistence is absent. Promise no work after the turn. A saved log does not prove automatic recovery. Inspect interrupted action identity and destination before replay; an unknown outcome blocks it.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nDependency setup, plugin installation, host enabling, personal settings, schedules, external writes and credentials need their own explicit grants. The operative checkout has no installed dependencies. The approved isolated snapshot 37b68c8e842b275f310ead112c0ecb7fa0ade308 passed 85 helper tests with 316 assertions and strict TypeScript with zero errors. That evidence proves only that snapshot. Pins are commander 14.0.0, bun-types 1.3.14 and typescript 7.0.2. The [helper setup guide](helper-setup.md) documents the exact historical copy and the separate approval boundary for any future setup. Future setup requires fresh authorization for an exact writable copy under Herd, registry https://registry.npmjs.org, --ignore-scripts and a task-owned cache. Ordinary helpers use Bun with --no-install and never bootstrap installation.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n      }\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n  },\\\\\\\\n  {\\\\\\\\n
